item.title: A first-time WNBA champion awaits as Valkyries, Dream open the Finals
item.description: Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese attempts a basket during a media day in Oakland, Calif., Friday, Oct. 16, 2026, ahead of Saturday's Game 1 of the WNBA basketball Finals against the Golden State Valkyries. (Yalonda M. James/San Francisco Chronicle via AP) Yalonda M. James The WNBA will crown a first-time champion with the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream playing for the title in the best-of-seven series that starts Saturday. [DOWNLOAD: Free WSB-TV News app for alerts as news breaks ] Golden State is looking to become the fastest expansion team in league history to win a championship as the Valkyries are only in their second year. Atlanta reached the Finals for the first time since 2013 and after losing in its previous three appearances in the championship round, will be trying for their first as well. Offense will be at a premium as the series features two of the best defensive teams in the league led by coaches Karl Smesko and Natalie Nakase . [M ORE: WNBA Finals: Watch the Atlanta Dream at these watch parties ] Finding the Finals For the first time in a long time, ESPN won’t be broadcasting the WNBA Finals. As part of the new media rights deal, NBC and USA Sports have the rights to the championship round. The two networks will be splitting it with NBC showing Game 1 on Saturday and Game 4 a week later. USA Network will have Game 2 and 3 as well as 5, 6 and 7 if they are necessary. Anaylst Sarah Kustok will be doing double-duty working for both networks. Hot ticket The WNBA Finals are a hot ticket with Golden State having the highest attendance during the regular season, averaging over 18,000 fans. The get-in price for Game 1 was just over $200 according to the website Gametime. Last year, Game 1 of the Finals between Phoenix and Las Vegas had a get-in price of $48 the day before the game. Atlanta was able to secure State Farm Arena for Game 3 and 4 after the WNBA and NBA came together to resolve conflicts at that arena. Had that not happened the team would have had to most likely play at Gateway Center Arena — its usual home that seats 3,500. Now they’ll play at the 17,000 seat venue that is the home of the Atlanta Hawks. As of now tickets for the two games in Atlanta are under $100, but that could change closer to game time. The Dream didn’t open the upper bowl of State Farm for their first three playoff games in the arena, but will do so for the Finals. [SIGN UP: WSB-TV Daily Headlines Newsletter ] Winning Angel Atlanta’s Angel Reese has won at every level she’s played at so far besides the WNBA. item.title: Alabama vs. Tennessee Livestream: How to Watch the Football Game Online Free
item.description: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Rolling Stone may receive an affiliate commission. College football fans are getting another edition of the Third Saturday in October this weekend with the No. 14 Tennessee Volunteers. hosting the No. 6 Alabama Crimson Tide in Knoxville. More from Rolling Stone WNBA Finals Livestream: How to Watch Dream vs. Valkyries Games Online Free The Best Celebrity and Pop-Culture Halloween Costumes, From Trendy to Timeless The Best Audiophile Headphones for Music The SEC powerhouses will enter Neyland Stadium with identical records — 5-1 overall, 3-1 SEC — and both will be looking to recover their confidence after less-than-stellar performances last weekend. Alabama suffered its first loss of the season, falling 20-17 to the top-ranked Georgia Bulldogs , and Tennessee cut it far too close with a 24-17 win against the unranked Arkansas Razorbacks. At a Glance: How to Watch Alabama vs. Tennessee Game TV channel : ABC Free stream : DirecTV , Fubo Date, time : Saturday, Oct. 17, at 3:30 p.m. ET stream free with directv Both teams will also be missing some key talent, with the Crimson Tide’s leading receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams and the Vols will be without quarterback Faizon Brandon. George MacIntyre will step in as starting QB for a second straight week. One of the biggest factors will be Tennessee’s home field advantage. The Vols have beaten the Tide the last two times Alabama visited Neyland, and they’re 32-8 at home since 2021. Still, oddsmakers are predicting that Bama will overcome the Vols’ energy, favoring the Tide by 7.5 points. For those who can’t make it to Neyland, ABC will handle a national broadcast . How to Watch Alabama vs. Tennessee Game: Channel, Date, Time This weekend’s Alabama vs. Tennessee college football game will take place on Saturday, Oct. 17. Kickoff is at 3:30 p.m. ET/12:30 p.m. PT. The game will be broadcast on ABC. Where to Stream Alabama vs. Tennessee Game Online Free If you don’t have cable, you can livestream the Alabama vs. Tennessee game online using any live TV streaming service that carries ABC. DirecTV , Fubo , Hulu + Live TV , and Sling are all great options. Those first two — DirecTV and Fubo — both offer free trials that you can use to watch Alabama vs. Tennessee for free online. Here are more details on how to get a free Alabama vs. Tennessee livestream with DirecTV and Fubo: EDITOR'S PICK DirecTV get free trial DirecTV carries ABC in all of its Signature Packages and its MyNews and MySports Genre Packs. Get a five-day free trial to any of these plans to stream Alabama vs. Tennessee for free (plus other football games this weekend). If you want to keep DirecTV after the trial, plans start at $44.99 a month, but you’ll also get a discount on your first month’s bill. Fubo get free trial Fans can also get a free Alabama vs. Tennessee stream with Fubo, which offers a five-day free trial and carries ABC in all plans. After the trial

item.title: Buccaneers’ Baker Mayfield is out vs. Steelers, but when could he return from injury?
item.description: Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Buccaneers’ Baker Mayfield is out vs. Steelers, but when could he return from injury? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will face the Pittsburgh Steelers without Baker Mayfield , but his return could be approaching. The Buccaneers quarterback continues to recover from a dislocated thumb , although optimism is growing about his availability next week. According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, Mayfield will miss his third consecutive game Sunday . However, there’s optimism that he could return against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7. That matchup would mark Tampa Bay’s first NFC South game of the season. It could also provide Mayfield with an opportunity to regain momentum after an extended absence. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The veteran quarterback suffered the injury during Tampa Bay’s Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. He dislocated his right thumb late in the fourth quarter. Subsequent medical testing revealed no additional damage, offering some encouragement about his recovery. However, Mayfield’s ability to grip and throw a football remains an important factor in determining his return. Head coach Todd Bowles recently acknowledged that Mayfield’s Week 7 availability was still uncertain. The Buccaneers have avoided rushing their starting quarterback into action. Earlier reports suggested Mayfield could miss three to six weeks, depending on his recovery progress. Meanwhile, rookie Jalon Daniels has stepped into the starting role during Mayfield’s absence. The Buccaneers backup quarterback has been preparing for another start against Pittsburgh. Daniels helped Tampa Bay secure a 24-16 victory over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 5. Mayfield’s potential return against Carolina would provide a timely boost as Tampa Bay begins divisional competition. For now, the Buccaneers must navigate another game without their starting quarterback. His progress next week will determine whether the anticipated return becomes reality. Related: Steelers Week 6 injury report vs. Buccaneers: What Rico Dowdle’s status means for Jaylen Warren fantasy owners Related: Buccaneers’ Baker Mayfield officially won’t play again in Week 6

item.title: Jake Fraser-McGurk blazes to 14-ball fifty in One-Day Cup, misses Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's world record
item.description: Australian batter Jake Fraser-McGurk produced a breathtaking display of power-hitting, smashing the fastest half-century in One-Day Cup history as South Australia posted a commanding 397/7 against Queensland at the Karen Rolton Oval in Adelaide on Saturday. The 24-year-old opener raced to his fifty in just 14 deliveries, breaking his own tournament record. He eventually scored 122 off 63 balls, hammering 10 fours and nine sixes to put South Australia in a dominant position. His effort also ranks among the joint fourth-fastest half-centuries in List A cricket, with India's Vaibhav Sooryavanshi holding the world record for the fastest fifty, off just 11 balls. Fraser-McGurk found an equally impressive partner in South Australia captain Nathan McSweeney, who registered his third List A century with a composed 106 off 103 balls. Their efforts helped the hosts finish with a formidable total in their 50 overs. Fraser-McGurk Goes on the Attack Fraser-McGurk wasted little time taking control of the innings. He plundered 22 runs from Tom Straker's second over before launching an assault on Tom Whitney in the fourth, striking two sixes and a four. The Australian brought up his half-century in the sixth over with a boundary off Hayden Kerr and continued his onslaught, racing to 75 off just 22 deliveries. With the fastest List A century in sight, he briefly threatened to surpass his own record of reaching three figures in 29 balls. However, after surviving a couple of chances, Fraser-McGurk tempered his aggression before accelerating again. He smashed two consecutive sixes off Whitney and brought up his century in just 49 deliveries. His explosive knock finally ended at 122 in the 21st over when Kerr dismissed him, but the opener had already provided South Australia with a flying start. McSweeney Provides Crucial Support While Fraser-McGurk supplied the fireworks, McSweeney anchored the innings with a well-paced century. The South Australia skipper struck 106 off 103 balls, reaching his third List A hundred and ensuring the hosts maintained their momentum after the opener's dismissal. Fraser-McGurk's performance also continued his remarkable record at the Karen Rolton Oval. Across six List A innings at the Adelaide venue, he has accumulated runs at an average of 68.66 and a strike rate of 204.97, including two centuries and a half-century. His record-breaking innings, combined with McSweeney's contribution, gave South Australia a strong platform as they finished on 397/7 against Queensland. 135014199

item.title: Four teams, two individuals bring home cross country titles to Richland County
item.description: It was a banner day for Richland County cross country teams. In all, four team won conference championships on Saturday, Oct. 17 and two runners won individual titles. Let's run down what all happened in the Ohio Cardinal Conference, Mid-Ohio Athletic Conference, Firelands Conference and Mid-Buckeye Conference. FOLLOW THE SEASON: 2026 Richland County Cross Country Scoreboard: Runners pass big tests before conference week Lexington sweeps Ohio Cardinal Conference championships In the girls race, the Lexington Lady Lex won the Ohio Cardinal Conference championship with just 26 team points. Gabi Twedt led Lady Lex in second place with an 18:27.38 while Jenna Halfhill was fourth with a 19:14.52, Evalynn Adkins was fifth with a 19:32.84, Adria Sharrock was seventh with a 20:38.39 and Nyra Loy was 10th with a 20:52.88 to round out the Top 5 runners for Lexington. It is Lexington’s 20 th league championship in program history and 19 th consecutive conference crown. The 2026 team joins team from 2005, 2007, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 to win league championships. The Madison Rams took seventh with 216 team points. Livia Grove led the Rams in 36th place with a 23:48.58 while Casey Rachel was 42nd with a 24:50.17, Natalie Smith was 45th with a 25:20.39, Mariah Stacy was 46th with a 25:24.76 and Chloe Jeffers was 47th with a 26:13.12 to round out the Top 5 runners Madison. In the boys race, the Lexington Minutemen made it a clean sweep winning the team title with 23 points. Will Hooper led the Minutemen by winning the individual OCC championship with a 15:58.11 while Christian Estep was second with a 16:07.29, John Bartone was third with a 16:13.32, Mathias Bender was fifth with a 16:38.77 and Chidalu Ezike was 12th with a 17:26.59 to round out the Top 5 runners for Lexington. The Minutemen won the 13 th league championship in program history and fifth consecutive conference crown joining teams from 2005, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2011, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. Madison took sixth as a team with 138 points. Evan Larsen led the Rams in eighth place with a 16:56.12 while Jackson Brummett was 17th with a 17:38.05, Gannon Conway was 26th with an 18:08.21, Alden Washington was 43rd with a 19:49.02 and Jonas Stapleton was 44th with a 19:58.15 to round out the Top 5 runners for Madison. Mansfield Senior finished eighth as a team with 222 points. Prince Converse led the Tygers in 35th place with an 18:38.87 while Gavin Camak was 36th with an 18:40.97, Tyler Hubbard was 48th with a 20:55.46, Christian Cole was 50th with a 21:04.86 and Xavier Kegley was 53rd with a 24:15.75 to round out the Top 5 runners for Mansfield Senior. item.title: Pressure grows on Renee Slegers as Arsenal booed off after Birmingham draw
item.description: Arsenal were held to a 1-1 draw by Birmingham City to extend their winless Women’s Super League run and increase the pressure on Renee Slegers. The Gunners have not won in the WSL since the opening day of the season and have now gone five games in the league without victory. Arsenal could be as many as 12 points behind leaders Manchester City if the champions beat Brighton on Sunday and they are almost certainly out of the title race already. Slegers led Arsenal to the Women’s Champions League in 2025 but the Gunners have been unable to kick on in the two WSL seasons since and challenge for the title. The hosts were booed off at the Emirates and it could have been worse after Olivia Smith’s stunning strike salvaged a point for them. Alessia Russo hit the crossbar late in the first half before Oceane Hurtre fired the visitors in front eight minutes after the restart. Arsenal visit north London rivals Tottenham Hotspur next week and will do so while trailing Spurs by at least four points in the table.

item.title: Bayern Munich vs. RB Leipzig: Gamethread
item.description: Photo by Carina Johansen / NTB / AFP via Getty Images / Norway OUT | NTB/AFP via Getty Images Lineups are out! Several midweek starters retain their place in the starting XI. Jonas Urbig, Kim Min-jae, and Nathaniel Brown all start this match along with Ismael Saibari. Alphonso Davies and Lennart Karl sit on the bench. ♦️ Mit dieser Startelf zum Heimsieg ♦️ #packmas #FCBRBL pic.twitter.com/7n5fVtKrNt — FC Bayern München (@FCBayern) October 17, 2026 Bayern Munich fell short in the Champions League, slumping to a 3-3 draw and saw Michael Olise get suspended just before Arsenal. Smarting from that horror show, the Bavarians welcome RB Leipzig in a clash between 3rd and 5th place in the Bundesliga. The Lawnballers enter this game with a spring in their step, having beaten Eintracht Frankfurt 6-0 last week; Die Roten Bullen scored twice in five minutes and lead 4-0 at the break, a clear indication of their quality. Bayern on the other hand hasn’t won a Bundesliga match since the 7-0 win over Union Berlin just before the international break. A team like Bayern should not be going almost a month without a league win. This match is the chance to correct that. Match Info Location : Allianz Arena, Munich, Bavaria, Germany Date : October 17, 2026 Kickoff : 6:30 PM Local time | 12:30 PM EST | 9:30 AM PST TV/streaming: Peacock (en español), USA/Fandango (United States — check listings) , Find Your Country SBN App: Engage with match threads on Bavarian Football Works from your phone with the new SB Nation app. Commenting and interacting with your communities is easier than ever before with the Game Chat feature. The app is available currently in the U.S. on iOS and Android devices. Prediction Bayern wins 3-0. Bayern will channel the anger of not winning in midweek and not having Olise against Arsenal and dominate Leipzig. Harry Kane, Michael Olise, and Serge Gnabry off the bench will score. item.title: Today’s Irish Fan Game Plan: Contain BYU’s Bear Bachmeier
item.description: Iowa State Cyclones' linebacker Caleb Bacon (26) and linebacker Kooper Ebel (47) takes down BYU Cougars quarterback Bear Bachmeier (47) during the first quarter at Jack Trice Stadium on Oct. 25, 2025, in Ames, Iowa. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co This week, One Foot Down asked our connected Notre Dame football fans to weigh in on what they say is the biggest obstacle to the Irish prevailing in Provo today. We heard from 53 respondents, and almost six out of every ten said: Box in Bear Bachmeier, beat BYU. Bachmeier is 77-for-106 for 1,o33 yards, with eight passing touchdowns against one interception. The sophomore can create chaos with his legs as well, rushing for 239 yards on 36 attempts and four additional touchdowns. The Irish haven’t yielded a rushing touchdown yet this year. Could the streak break today at Bachmeier’s behest? About one-quarter of respondents said they thought the altitude would be the Irish’s Provo problem. LaVell Edwards Stadium sits 4,649 feet above sea level, which is the eighth highest in college football. For comparison, the Irish play their home games at Notre Dame Stadium, which sits about 723 feet above sea level. Will the Irish be left gasping for breath as BYU runs tempo? And will this be most apparent in the first quarter, the fourth, or never at all? Just four percent of respondents picked the Cougars running backs, but I do have to wonder if that percentage would have been far greater if BYU’s best, L.J. Martin, were playing today. Martin, the Big 12’s Offensive Player of the Year in 2025, leads the team in rushing with 344 yards on 44 attempts. He also caught five balls for 41 yards as a receiver. The Cougars will rely today on redshirt junior Preston Rex and freshmen Journee Tonga and DeVaughn Eka. On this week’s podcast , Joshua, Brendan and myself all picked Notre Dame to cover the 10.5 point spread. Now is your time to weigh in. You can head over to FanDuel , the sponsor of this post, and lock in your pick and you can leave it in the comments below.

The Minnesota Vikings continued to evaluate their wide receiver depth during the bye week by bringing in JuJu Smith-Schuster for a workout following their 23-13 victory over the New Orleans Saints. The veteran wide receiver, who has experience with the Pittsburgh Steelers, Kansas City Chiefs, and New England Patriots, has not yet been signed by Minnesota. The concerns about wide receiver depth arise from injuries to Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, as well as Jauan Jennings’ unexpectedly limited role over the first five games. However, the Vikings’ trade deadline priorities should extend beyond merely adding another pass catcher. Their unbeaten start has shown that the defense is capable of controlling games, while injuries along the offensive line and a young defensive front have exposed areas where added experience could prove valuable as the schedule becomes more challenging. With that, three players stand out as particularly sensible targets for the Vikings. Vasquez-Imagn Images The Chargers’ 0-5 start has put Khalil Mack at the center of trade speculation, and the Minnesota Vikings should have a legitimate interest in the veteran edge rusher. Mack re-signed with Los Angeles on a one-year deal during the offseason, and his contract does not include a no-trade clause. At 35 years old, his value is more closely tied to helping a contender over the next few months than to a rebuilding team, which makes the Chargers’ poor performance particularly relevant as the trade deadline of November 10 approaches. Minnesota would provide a very different environment for him. Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel already form the foundation of the Vikings’ edge rusher group, while defensive coordinator Brian Flores has built a defense that relies heavily on disguise, movement, and pressure from multiple alignments. Mack would fit into this system without having to shoulder the entire pass rush, allowing Minnesota to manage his workload while creating more challenging protection decisions for opposing offenses. The need for Mack becomes even stronger when considering the departure of Jonathan Greenard during the offseason. Turner has been tasked with taking on more responsibility in his third season, and Minnesota has received valuable contributions from other young defenders, but adding a proven veteran like Mack would provide Flores with another option for obvious passing situations without hindering the development of the players already in place. Mack’s experience also holds value beyond just sacks. Having spent over a decade dealing with protection adjustments, chips, and double teams, he would give Minnesota another defender capable of recognizing how offenses are attempting to neutralize pressure before the play develops. The Chargers would likely seek draft picks in exchange for Mack from multiple contenders, so the Vikings should remain disciplined during negotiations. A veteran on an expiring contract should not command the same type of return as a younger foundational pass rusher. Minnesota’s leverage comes from already having one of the league’s better defenses rather than needing a trade to stay competitive. A reasonable price could turn an already difficult defensive front into an even deeper unit for the final months of the season. Daron Payne would bring proven interior power to a young defensive line Geoff Burke-Imagn Images In the 2026 draft, Minnesota made significant investments in the defensive interior by selecting Caleb Banks in the first round and Domonique Orange on Day 2. These additions provided defensive coordinator Brian Flores with a much younger group, following the departures of Jonathan Allen and Javon Hargrave, but the Vikings are still relying on developing players to take on meaningful snaps during a season that has quickly evolved into a legitimate contention window. Daron Payne would bring a different type of presence to the team. The Washington Commanders have started the season poorly with a record of 1-3-1, and Payne has already been mentioned in trade discussions as the team evaluates a veteran player who is in the final year of his contract. At 29 years old, he still can disrupt the pocket from the interior, having recorded a sack and a forced fumble against the Giants in Week 5. His strength against the run would also provide Minnesota with another option alongside Jalen Redmond and Levi Drake Rodriguez. Payne would fit well within Flores’ system because he possesses the athleticism to play multiple positions along the defensive front, rather than being confined to one spot. The Vikings frequently alter their defensive alignments before the snap, and an interior defender capable of attracting multiple blockers would help create clearer paths for the linebackers and edge rushers around him. Adding Payne would also alleviate some of the pressure on Banks and Orange, allowing both rookies to remain part of the rotation while learning from a veteran who has extensive experience in playoff races, heavy workloads, and various defensive schemes. Donte Jackson could give the secondary more veteran stability Scott Galvin-Imagn Images Minnesota’s cornerback situation entered the season with limited depth behind starters Byron Murphy Jr. and Isaiah Rodgers, and the first month has not alleviated those concerns. Rookie Chuck Demmings has already faced a hamstring injury, while James Pierre and Zemaiah Vaughn have been called upon to support the starting duo. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores’ system places significant responsibility on defensive backs due to the extensive use of disguise and man coverage, and this makes experience particularly valuable as offenses begin to exploit weaker areas. Donte Jackson, a cornerback from the Los Angeles Chargers, could become available as the team evaluates veteran contracts in the upcoming weeks. At 30 years old, Jackson has extensive starting experience, recording nine interceptions over the past two seasons, including four with the Chargers in 2025. This year, although limited due to a hamstring injury, he has also broken up two passes and forced a fumble. Any potential acquisition would require a careful assessment of his health, but the fit seems logical for Minnesota. Jackson would provide an experienced option at outside cornerback without disrupting the roles of Murphy and Rodgers. This flexibility would be beneficial for the coaching staff, especially if injuries or specific matchups necessitate heavier rotation. Given the Chargers’ current record, an experienced cornerback on a short-term deal may be obtainable for modest compensation. Minnesota can afford to think like a buyer A 5-0 record does not necessitate the Vikings becoming reckless before the trade deadline, especially given that injuries have already tested several areas of the roster. The front office has continued to make smaller adjustments, such as the Smith-Schuster workout and recent practice squad additions, but Kevin O’Connell has used the bye week to evaluate a team that has won despite rarely having all preferred starters available simultaneously. All this success and instability gives Minnesota a clear reason to remain active. item.title: How to watch Rutgers vs Maryland: Live stream NCAA College Football, TV channel
item.description: A pair of teams looking for their first Big Ten Conference win collide on Saturday when the Rutgers Scarlet Knights (1-4) visit the Maryland Terrapins (2-4), with the Terps riding a four-game losing streak. A scuffle breaks out on the Ohio State Buckeyes bench near the end of the NCAA football game against the Maryland Terrapins at Ohio Stadium in Columbus on Oct. 10, 2026. How to Watch Rutgers vs Maryland When: Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 Time: 12:30 PM ET TV Channel: Big Ten Network Live Stream: Fubo ( try for free ) Maryland fell to 0-3 in the Big Ten with a 45-16 loss at then-No. 5 Ohio State last week. Malik Washington got the Terrapins to within 14-10 with a five-yard touchdown run in the second quarter before the Buckeyes pulled away for a 31-10 halftime lead. Daniel Wingate scored the other Maryland touchdown, returning an interception 52 yards to the house late in the third quarter. The Terps managed only 146 yards of total offense inb the loss. Rutgers returns from a bye week on the heels of a 47-15 loss to then-No. 6 Indiana on Oct. 3. The Scarlet Knights trailed 37-0 before backup quarterback AJ Surace found Ben Black III for a 53-yard scoring pass late in the third quarter. Clay Thevenin added a one-yard TD run early in the fourth for Rutgers. Surace threw for 128 yards on 6-of-10 passing after starter Dylan Lonergan went down with a head injury in the second quarter. The Scarlet Knights won the last two meetings against the Terrapins, including a 35-20 win at home on Nov. 8, while Maryland leads the series 12-9. Washington enters the game with 1,352 yards and seven touchdown passes with six interceptions while Chris Durr Jr. has 46 receptions for 476 yards and four scores. In four games, Lonergan has 775 yards with seven TDs and five picks, with Antwan Raymond leading the ground attack with 469 yards and four touchdowns. KJ Duff comes in with 33 catches, 628 yards and seven scores. This is a great college football matchup that you will not want to miss; make sure to tune in and catch all the action. The Scarlet Knights won the last two meetings against the Terrapins, including a 35-20 win at home on Nov. 8, while Maryland leads the series 12-9. Washington enters the game with 1,352 yards and seven touchdown passes with six interceptions while Chris Durr Jr. has 46 receptions for 476 yards and four scores. In four games, Lonergan has 775 yards with seven TDs and five picks, with Antwan Raymond leading the ground attack with 469 yards and four touchdowns. KJ Duff comes in with 33 catches, 628 yards and seven scores. This is a great college football matchup that you will not want to miss; make sure to tune in and catch all the action. item.title: 10 Atlanta Falcons Prospects to Watch For Week 7 of College Football
item.description: Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to the meat and potatoes of the college football season. This Saturday, the cream of the crop will show up in multiple ranked matchups, along with a few ranked-vs.-unranked games featuring real talent that may pop up in the 2027 NFL Draft. With most of the cupcakes out of the way, several draft picks have big games ahead in Week 7 of college football, but here are 10 prospects Atlanta Falcons fans should watch. Nick Marsh, WR, Indiana vs. Ohio State Memorial Stadium – Bloomington, IN – 12 pm EST – Fox Nick Marsh route salesmanship. Very snappy mover at 6025 & his head fakes at the top of the stem are so convincing pic.twitter.com/QeOrGcF5Ex — James Foster (@NoFlagsFilm) October 6, 2026 While Charlie Becker may be the more well-rounded prospect, Nick Marsh has the tools a quarterback like Michael Penix might find appealing. He wins on out-breaking routes; he snaps his head and hips at the top of the route, forcing separation and making himself an immediate target for quarterbacks who throw with anticipation, like Penix. Overall, Marsh projects as a solid X or Z receiver in a Tommy Rees offense, allowing Drake London to move around the formations and unlock even more production. Emmanuel Oyebadejo, DL, Florida @ Texas DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium – Austin, TX – 12 pm EST – ABC Florida DL Emmanuel Oyebadejo (6'6 299) was a basketball player in England before giving football a try first at University of Exeter, then Jacksonville state and now Florida He's still very raw but he also shows the traits of a starting NFL DL. Size/Power/Athleticism #NFLDraft pic.twitter.com/rtJt1NIDgj — Draft Capital Podcast (@TheDraftCapital) September 20, 2026 6’6”, 300 pounds is not supposed to move as it does for Florida defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo. A former English basketball player, Oyebadejo is still a raw prospect who needs to learn some of the nuances of the defensive line. However, Oyebadejo already has the raw movement skills, power, and quickness needed to be a high-end prospect. Isaac Smith, S, Mississippi State @ LSU Tiger Stadium – Baton Rouge, LA – 12 pm EST – ESPN Isaac Smith from Mississippi State is a massive dude for a safety. I have some concerns about the lateral agility and overall athleticism for sticking at safety, so a move to linebacker could make some sense for the next level. pic.twitter.com/Wmn20bnQsu — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) May 20, 2026 Having a big body at safety is always an advantage; when that safety can play the run like a linebacker, it adds another layer of versatility to the defense. Isaac Smith is a big safety at 6’0”, 220 pounds, and he can come in on day one and add to the special teams unit with his ability to find a ball carrier and bring him to the turf. Xavier Gilliam, DT, Tennessee vs. Alabama Neyland Stadium – Knoxville, TN – 3:30 pm EST – ABC The Xavier Gilliam Auburn tape is some pretty electric stuff for an IDL

Gervon Dexter and Brandon Dorlus are two of the best at the position right now at getting pressure on the quarterback, but adding a rookie like Xavier Gilliam to the rotation would be a dream come true. I’m throwing all of that away because of how Penn State’s Audavion Collins has played heading into this week. Listed at 5’11”, 185 pounds, he has allowed only two catches on seven targets through six games and has showcased elite speed and footwork that keep him in position to make a play on the ball. Evan Johnson, CB, BYU vs. Notre Dame LaVell Edwards Stadium – Provo, UT – 7:30 pm EST – ABC BYU CB Evan Johnson ( @__Evxn ) had a breakout year for the Cougars, earning Honorable Mention All-Big 12 honors. Listed at 6'0", 185 lbs, the Monterey, California native recorded 47 tackles (2 TFLs), a sack, 8 PBUs, and a team-leading 5 interceptions. Look for Johnson and… pic.twitter.com/iyedxjtbY7 — Bryan (@RealBGauvin23) May 1, 2026 Coming into this season, one of the hotter names at cornerback was Evan Johnson, especially after his Pop-Tart Bowl performance, where he allowed only one catch on six targets and recorded an interception. At 6’0”, 181 pounds, Johnson has had a fine start to the 2026 season, but he gets the Notre Dame Fighting Irish and superstar quarterback C.J. Carr in primetime. This could be a breakout game in a big moment for BYU. Patrick Overmyer, TE, Houston vs. Oklahoma State TDECU Stadium – Houston, TX – 7:30 pm EST – Fox Je vous en ai déjà parlé plusieurs fois, Patrick Overmyer continue son excellente saison du côté de Houston. 9rec 83yds 4 TD (ça aurait pu être 5 si Weigman ne s'était pas manqué) face à Kansas State. Le problème est son run block qui va fortement baissé son draft stock. pic.twitter.com/K69YmKbkkS — Valentin (@ScoutValentin) October 15, 2026 If the Falcons want to add more of a receiving option to the tight end room, Houston’s Patrick Overmyer would be a great addition. Last week against Kansas State, he had nine receptions for 83 yards and four touchdowns, all in the red zone. Atlanta could use another consistent red zone threat like Overmyer, especially if he can show more as a run blocker before the year ends. Coleton Price, C, Kentucky @ Oklahoma Memorial Stadium – Norman, OK – 7:30 pm EST – SEC Network Coleton Price finding work & clearing the pocket #slab pic.twitter.com/tQT1BHYU2v — Brandon Thorn (@BrandonThornNFL) September 22, 2026 I understand that Ryan Neuzil is putting some of his best work on tape, but he still is going to be a free agent next season, and who knows if Ian Cunningham and company will pay the premium that may be necessary to keep him in house. If they want to look in a different direction, Kentucky’s Coleton Price may be an avenue to explore, especially if he has a good day against Oklahoma’s David Stone. item.title: Chiefs need to stay on their toes against winless Chargers
item.description: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s hard to call a division matchup a trap game, but the (4-0) Kansas City Chiefs must avoid overlooking the winless Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday afternoon. According to Tom Pelissero, formerly of NFL Network , now with The Ringer and Netflix , the Chargers are “rejecting trade calls” because the team believes it is close to turning it around after an 0-5 start. There are no plans for “a fire sale.” That narrative could change if the Chiefs take care of business this weekend, but if Kansas City lets Los Angeles get its bounceback performance and pick up a win in the AFC West along the way, it could be the turning point the Chargers need to regroup. Head coach Andy Reid understands the Chargers’ desperation. A Reid-led Chiefs team once started 1-5 before ripping off enough consecutive wins to make the postseason in 2015. During his press conference on Friday, Reid warned that Kansas City needs to stay alert and avoid getting caught off guard by an offensive mind looking to manufacture a win with a lengthy injury report . “Well, you expect the unexpected,” Reid said when asked about Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. “He’s a sharp mind and very creative, so you’ve got to be on your toes. He does a nice job. (Chargers Head Coach) Jim (Harbaugh), likewise. I mean, you have two guys in there that are real good football guys, offensive minds.” Los Angeles will be without its two starting offensive tackles — Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater — along with its top wideout this year: Tre Harris. It’s hard to know what the unit could look like with all the injuries, and the Chargers could play into the ambiguity to pull off a major upset. With their season at a clear pivot point ahead of a Week 7 bye, Los Angeles will go all-out for a win in Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday. On offense, defense and special teams, the Chiefs must be prepared for anything, because the Chargers will play like they have nothing to lose.

item.title: Arsenal at Nottingham Forest Premier League match preview: Sharpen the axe
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 13: Jurrien Timber of Arsenal celebrates with team mates after he scored for 1-0 during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between Arsenal FC and LOSC Lille at Arsenal Stadium on October 13, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Shaun Brooks - CameraSport via Getty Images) | CameraSport via Getty Images Arsenal head north to take on Nottingham Forest on Sunday in the Premier League ahead of a marquee Champions League match at Bayern Munich next week. The Gunners have enjoyed their return to action following the first international break. It hasn’t been smooth sailing, but they have certainly gotten back to business since their 0-3 loss at Brighton. A nervier-than-it-needed-to-be, come-from behind win against Leeds was followed up by a dominant 3-0 win against Lille in the CL where Mikel Arteta’s side looked confident and in control from start to finish. You can’t quantify or measure momentum, but you can sure as hell sense it. If there’s a criticism to be laid upon the Gunners so far this season, it is that they haven’t taken matches by the scruff and imposed themselves consistently when the opportunities present themselves. There have been plenty of moments of brilliance, but it hasn’t felt like they have had that “oh, wait, we’re the champions of England” epiphany just yet. With that being said, you can’t argue with the results. Eight wins from nine matches is excellent. Clearly, they are efficient and get the job done. Teams have brought their best against the defending title holders, which was always going to be the case. The target on their backs has never been bigger, and they have done what they needed to take care of business. But would it kill them to be just a little more assertive and stamp their names on matches? Heading to Forest on the heels of their first one-sided performance in a while is going to be a test of their ability to seize momentum. With a big CL match away to Bayern Munich on deck, building on Wednesday’s performance and capitalizing on the opportunity is paramount. Can they do it? That’s the question. Between their megalomaniacal owner publicly inserting himself into the Morgan Gibbs-White transfer saga, the end of the disastrous tenure of former Arsenal Head of Football Operations Edu, and enduring
item.content:encoded: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 13: Jurrien Timber of Arsenal celebrates with team mates after he scored for 1-0 during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between Arsenal FC and LOSC Lille at Arsenal Stadium on October 13, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Shaun Brooks - CameraSport via Getty Images) | CameraSport via Getty Images Arsenal head north to take on Nottingham Forest on Sunday in the Premier League ahead of a marquee Champions League match at Bayern Munich next week. The Gunners have enjoyed their return to action following the first international break. It hasn’t been smooth sailing, but they have certainly gotten back to business since their 0-3 loss at Brighton. A nervier-than-it-needed-to-be, come-from behind win against Leeds was followed up by a dominant 3-0 win against Lille in the CL where Mikel Arteta’s side looked confident and in control from start to finish. You can’t quantify or measure momentum, but you can sure as hell sense it. If there’s a criticism to be laid upon the Gunners so far this season, it is that they haven’t taken matches by the scruff and imposed themselves consistently when the opportunities present themselves. There have been plenty of moments of brilliance, but it hasn’t felt like they have had that “oh, wait, we’re the champions of England” epiphany just yet. With that being said, you can’t argue with the results. Eight wins from nine matches is excellent. Clearly, they are efficient and get the job done. Teams have brought their best against the defending title holders, which was always going to be the case. The target on their backs has never been bigger, and they have done what they needed to take care of business. But would it kill them to be just a little more assertive and stamp their names on matches? Heading to Forest on the heels of their first one-sided performance in a while is going to be a test of their ability to seize momentum. With a big CL match away to Bayern Munich on deck, building on Wednesday’s performance and capitalizing on the opportunity is paramount. Can they do it? That’s the question. Know the Enemy Domestic Record: 1W-2D-3L (15th) Arsenal vs Nottingham Forest all-time record: 56W-24D-29L Incomings: Liam Delap (Chelsea), Ousmane Diomande (Sporting), Daniel Muñonz (Crystal Palace), Gustavo Sá (Famalicão), Xaver Schlager (Leipzig), Steven Benda (Fulham) Departures: Elliot Anderson (Manchester City), Taiwo Awoniyi (Coventry), David Carmo (Olympiacos), Jota Silva (Olympiacos), Omar Richards (Aris Saloniki), Stefan Ortega (Olympiacos), Angus Gunn (San Jose Earthquakes) Injuries & Suspensions: Igor Jesus (calf), Nicolo Savona (knee), Nikola Milenkovic (knee), Morgan Gibbs-White (knock) The Tricky Trees made headlines for all of the wrong reasons last season. Between their megalomaniacal owner publicly inserting himself into the Morgan Gibbs-White transfer saga, the end of the disastrous tenure of former Arsenal Head of Football Operations Edu, and enduring a coaching carousel of four (!) different managers, the product on the pitch felt like a footnote compared to the drama that permeated the club, and the results reflected that as they tumbled to a 16th place finish on the heels of a 7th place finish the season prior. The hiring of former Crystal Palace manager Oliver Glasner over the summer looked a shrewd bit of business by Forest as they looked to right their reeling ship. After stamping his name in the Palace history books by leading the Eagles to an FA Cup in 2024/25 and a Conference League title in 25/26, his decision to part ways with the London club at the end of last season was made all the more perplexing when he agreed to manage Forest, who finished one spot below Palace and only 5 points clear of relegation. Like too many managers before him, his Forest tenure has been underwhelming so far. Through six Premier League matches, they have struggled to secure results with one win to their name, while their Carabao Cup campaign ended swiftly after a third round loss to Leeds in August. The Elliot Anderson-sized hole in their midfield has been hard to fill after the England international left for sportswashing mega-cheats Manchester City over the summer, but that was always going to be the case. Their early woes aren’t nearly as bad as they look. No team in the league has had as much bad luck in front of goal as they have, as evidenced by 5 goals scored from an xG of 10.30. Their finishing woes are not for lack of trying; they’ve taken the third most shots in the league (106) while also having the joint most shots hit the post (6). The only team with a worse conversion rate have been chronic underachievers Spurs. According to Opta’s expected league table , they are the season’s top under-performer so far, with the stat house having them theoretically 12 spots higher in third place. Their defensive returns have been equally as frustrating. They have faced only one shot (65) more than Arsenal, who have given up a league-low 64, while allowing only 22 shots on target, which is third-best in the PL and only three more than the Gunners. They have allowed a respectable 8 goals, but their inability to finish their dinner in the attack has undercut an otherwise solid defense. The availability of talisman Gibbs-White could be a potential problem for both sides. He suffered a muscular injury last week in Forest’s 1-3 defeat at Crystal Palace with his fitness for Sunday uncertain. Glasner’s pre-match comments seem to indicate that his injury isn’t serious and that he has a decent chance of making the match-day squad. With attacker Igor Jesus already out, Glasner may be forced to take a gamble on a not-fully-fit Gibbs-White, and for good reason. He is one of the league’s top facilitators so far, with the second most chances created (17), most big chances created (7), and most expected assists (1.87). Nottingham Forest are a team that is due a course correction on both ends of the pitch. Hopefully, that begins after Sunday. How Forest Can Win Where they will look to make a difference against Arsenal will be in the air and shooting from distance. They have won 52.8% of their aerial duels and have the second-most attempted headers with 20, bolstered by Morgan Gibbs-White and Neco Williams providing the second and third-most successful crosses across the Prem this season. Their penchant for long shots could trouble David Raya and the Gunners’ defense with over 40 shots from outside the box this season. Arsenal have struggled with long shots, having conceded 40% of their goals from distance. If they take them early and often, they could potentially find some success on the score sheet. How Arsenal Can Win Score, and score early. Simple, right? Arsenal’s biggest issue this season has been their slow starts. In eight matches across all competitions, the Gunners have scored a first-half goal in only 3 of them, with 5 of their 18 goals coming before halftime. They have also fallen behind in three of their last four Premier League matches before coming from behind to win two. Arsenal are fortunate in that their depth and overall quality gives them an edge as games wear on, but leaving it late and having to claw out of deficits is an awful trait to sustain for player and fan health alike. The last two matches between the Gunners and Forest at the City Ground have ended in goalless draws, and the Gunners have won just once in their last six visits. Getting off the mark early has to be a priority if they want to leave with all 3 points and keep pace with Manchester City. For Arsenal’s injuries, suspensions, & predicted lineups, make sure to check out our article here . WHO: Arsenal at Nottingham Forest WHAT: Premier League match day 7 WHEN: Sunday, October 18th, 11:30am EST/8:30am PST/4:30pm GMT WHERE: The City Ground, Nottingham HOW TO WATCH: Streaming on the Peacock app For all your international streaming needs, check LiveSoccerTV.com . item.title: How to watch the Valkyries vs Dream Game 1 without cable today
item.description: SFGate and Yahoo may earn commission from links in this article. Pricing and availability are subject to change. The Golden State Valkyries host the Atlanta Dream in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals at Chase Center. (Billy Cadden) The Golden State Valkyries have only been in the WNBA for two seasons, and they're already four wins away from a championship. After sweeping the defending champion Las Vegas Aces in the semifinals, the Valkyries return to Chase Center on Saturday for Game 1 of the WNBA Finals against the Atlanta Dream. It's a remarkable run for a franchise that didn't even exist on the court two years ago, and the Bay Area now gets to watch its newest basketball team compete for a championship with home-court advantage. The Dream won't be an easy final obstacle, either. Atlanta swept the New York Liberty in the semifinals and enters the Finals undefeated in the postseason, with Defensive Player of the Year Angel Reese leading the charge. But Golden State won all three regular-season meetings against Atlanta, and Gabby Williams has been playing some of her best basketball when it matters most. Neither franchise has ever won a WNBA championship, so history will be made regardless of the outcome. Valkyries fans hope this incredible run ends with a trophy coming home to San Francisco. The WNBA Finals tip off Saturday at 12:30 p.m. PDT at Chase Center, and basketball fans across the country can tune in with Sling TV and Peacock . When is the Valkyries vs. Dream Game 1? What : Golden State Valkyries vs. Atlanta Dream - WNBA Finals Game 1 When : Saturday, October 17, 2026 at 12:30 p.m. PDT Where : Chase Center, San Francisco, CA TV : NBC and Peacock How to stream the Valkyries vs. Aces Dream Game 1 without cable The Golden State Valkyries are just four wins away from a championship in their second season, and Bay Area fans can watch Game 1 of the WNBA Finals against the Atlanta Dream on Sling TV . Saturday's opener airs on NBC, which Sling carries in select markets, so check your zip code on Sling's website before signing up. Peacock is another excellent option, especially if you're planning to watch the entire Finals. Peacock streams every game in the best-of-seven series, with Premium starting at $12.99/month and Premium Plus at $19.99/month. Both plans include live sports, but Premium Plus also offers fewer ads on most other content and additional features. Peacock TV - Plans - peacocktv.com 9.99 Shop Now Sling is still a great choice if you want more live TV beyond the Finals. While Games 1 and 4 are on NBC, up to five other games will air on USA Network, which is included with Sling Blue and Orange & Blue. That means fans with either package can follow the entire series on Sling, as long as their local NBC station is available. item.title: WNBA fans can’t believe controversial referee has been picked for Dream vs. Valkyries finals clash
item.description: Photo by Brett Davis/Getty Images The WNBA Finals are set to take place as the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries will face off against each other in a quest to win their first-ever championship in franchise history. After a wait of almost over a week, Game 1 will tip off on Saturday in San Francisco. There is a lot of excitement to see who emerges victorious, as both teams have had brilliant runs to get to the WNBA Finals. There has been a lot of controversy ahead of the Finals, as Atlanta was unable to find a suitable arena to host fans for the games. However, after finding a solution to that, the latest WNBA Finals officials list caused another controversy, especially after fans saw the name of an infamous referee who has been in the news a lot lately. Fans fuming as Kevin Fahy named as one of the WNBA Officials for Finals The WNBA announced the list of officials for the Finals just two days ahead of Game 1. It was all good, until fans saw Kevin Fahy’s name on the list. The referee came under scrutiny for a missed timeout call he made during the Atlanta Dream vs. New York Liberty series. Breanna Stewart made it clear that she had asked Fahy if the Liberty had a timeout, but the three-time WNBA champion was firmly denied, which led to an attempted heave on the final play instead of advancing the ball beyond the half-court. After the game, the league put out a statement, which further caused a lot of anger among fans. “At that moment, there were multiple overlapping conversations and non-verbal exchanges between the referees, game participants, and also Stewart with Liberty bench personnel, which led to a misunderstanding amongst the various parties. Our referees can certainly handle these interactions better and have been given that feedback,” the statement from the league read. Not even a month later, seeing Fahy, who was responsible for the controversy on the WNBA Finals officials list led to a lot of criticism among fans. “Having Kevin on this list is malpractice,” said one fan. While another added: “The ref who told the Liberty they didn’t have a reset timeout, then later lied about it, just got chosen to work the finals. Your league is an absolute joke.” There were a few other referees as well, whom fans were not too pleased to see on the list. “So Timothy Green “doesn’t know the rules” & Kevin Fahy “no reset timeout” are on this list?!? Who in the @WNBA @WNBACommisioner allowed them after the glaring errors,” wrote one X user. Someone else stated: “I see every horrible official in the last Dream/Mystics and Dream/Liberty games are all included. They literally called 92 fouls between those two games. One game, a total of 56 alone.” An account user also opined: “it’s not too late to ask FIBA for their refs.” The officials for the Finals are selected by the WNBA Referee Operations Management Team. Bethany Donaphin, Head of WNBA League Operations, said: “This group of officials has earned the right to represent the WNBA and their profes

item.title: Washington Commanders Rumor Offers MAJOR Update on What Gets Dan Quinn Fired in Week 6
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Washington Commanders better not have any notable mental lapses in Week 6, because a new rumor claims it is sure to cost Dan Quinn his job as head coach. After Washington went 12-5 and reached the NFC Championship Game in the 2024 season, it seemed like the team had found the coach who could make them a consistent playoff contender. However, ever since, the Commanders have regressed. Last season, they finished with a disappointing 5-12 record. Many chalked it up to injuries — specifically to quarterback Jayden Daniels. However, there were some worrisome signs during the 2025 campaign. It put added pressure on the coach to deliver better results in 2026. However, they are 1-3-1 heading into a Week 6 Monday Night Football clash against the San Francisco 49ers . Their record is bad, but they seemingly hit a low point in the Quinn era last week when the offense completely lost track of how much time was left on the clock in overtime against the New York Giants and blew a chance at a game-winning field goal. Washington Commanders would need to be blown out by San Francisco 49ers to fire Dan Quinn Oct 4, 2026; Tottenham, ENG; Washington Commanders owner Josh Harris poses for a photo with fans before the game between Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images It has only reignited the discourse about the 56-year-old’s job security and the idea that he could be the first coach fired in-season. However, according to Tom Pelissero, while owner Josh Harris will be “paying close attention” on Monday night, he “ has never been a believer in midseason coaching changes .” That is why the NFL insider added that unless the Commanders suffer a blowout loss (very possible against a very good 49ers team) or there are obvious signs the team has quit on their coach, “expect Quinn to get the rest of the season to show he can get things turned in the right direction.” Furthermore, Daniels threw his support behind his coach after he mismanaged their final drive in Week 5, and the NFL insider claims, “Quinn has always had great command of the locker room.” Related Headlines Los Angeles Chargers Rumor Offers Surprising Update About Possible Fire Sale With Week 6 Loss 49ers Eyeing Blockbuster Trade for Former NFL Defensive Player of the Year as Super Bowl Push Intensifies Latest Week 6 NFL Injury Updates Before Tomorrow’s Games, Including Patriots Finally Getting AJ Brown Back Read more at Sportsnaut

item.title: Union Berlin hold blunt Dortmund attack in scoreless stalemate
item.description: Union Berlin hold blunt Dortmund attack in scoreless stalemate In an atmospheric Stadion an der Alten Försterei in Köpenick, Niko Kovač's Borussia Dortmund couldn't get the better of a rugged 1.FC Union Berlin side in the German capital. In the end, both sides had to settle for a point as it finished in a 0-0 stalemate. After the pyrotechnic smoke passed handful of late tackles from BVB trio Ethan Nwaneri, Waldemar Anton and Serhou Guirassy saw all three pick up early yellow cards. In truth, there was little to discuss in the initial 20 minutes with chances few and far better. Frederik Rønnow's goal came under a barrage of crosses, but the Dane handled each situation admirably. Barring one half-chance for Guirassy and a couple of Tim Skarke snipes at the other end, neither side could make serious inroads towards scoring. Union Berlin ended the first-half on the front foot, but the second half saw Lustrinelli bring on Emmanuel Latte Lath for Imeri. The move did little to reduce Skarke's attacking output. Another good opportunity fell the 30-year-old's way but he blazed over the top. The introduction of Kostas Karetsas and Fábio Silva was expected to lift the energy levels. Instead, the Greek prodigy hobbled off eight minutes later with an ankle injury. Kovač's remonstrations with the fourth official highlighting just how scrappy it had become. In the end, neither side managed to land a decisive blow in normal time or the five minutes of injury time provided. Once again, Dortmund's lack of cutting edge laid bare. Accompanying the scoreless draw, a share of the spoils for the first time ever in this fixture.

item.title: Borussia Dortmund draw with Union Berlin, leaving top spot at risk 🇩🇪
item.description: Borussia Dortmund draw with Union Berlin, leaving top spot at risk 🇩🇪 Borussia Dortmund drew 0-0 with Union Berlin—a good result... for Freiburg and Bayern Munich. Dortmund still lead the Bundesliga, now with 14 points, but could be overtaken later in the matchday. Watch the highlights soon. Freiburg (second with 13 points) visit Bayer Leverkusen at 10:30 a.m. on Sunday (18). Bayern (third with 11 points), meanwhile, host RB Leipzig at 1:30 p.m. this Saturday (17). Dortmund had plenty of the ball (64% possession), but played at a slow tempo and created little. BVB managed six shots over the 90 minutes—just one of them on target. Elversberg ⚔️ Augsburg Another of the Bundesliga's surprise packages, Elversberg raced into a 3-0 lead in the first half, endured a nervy finish and won 3-2. Elversberg climbed to sixth, in the Conference League spot, with 10 points. Augsburg sit ninth with eight. Schalke ⚔️ Mainz One of the Bundesliga's surprise packages, Mainz beat Schalke 1-0 away from home, with Phillip Tietz scoring in the first half. The result moved Mainz into the Europa League places, in fifth with 10 points. Schalke, meanwhile, remain 14th with five. Other matches 🇩🇪 Hamburg beat Stuttgart 1-0 thanks to a late goal from Miro Muheim. Werder Bremen and Paderborn, meanwhile, drew 2-2 after the visitors had taken a 2-0 lead. item.title: Tietz strike proves decisive as Mainz edge past Schalke
item.description: Tietz strike proves decisive as Mainz edge past Schalke Making the trip to Gelsenkirchen, Mainz carried a fantastic away record into the weekend, with their two wins this season both coming on their travels. And typically, Urs Fischer's side made an electric start and could have taken the lead inside the opening minute, with former Nullfünfer Loris Karius producing three impressive saves to deny Sheraldo Becker twice and Jae-sung Lee from the rebound. Miron Muslic's side gradually settled into the encounter, although clear-cut opportunities remained scarce, with Adil Aouchiche failing to pick out Edin Džeko after finding space down the left in the 12th minute. But Schalke continued to struggle in the final third before the visitors eventually broke the deadlock in the 24th minute after Kaishu Sano intercepted a Schalke clearance on the edge of the penalty area. The Japanese midfielder found Anthony Caci on the right, whose low delivery towards the near post Tietz met, guiding the ball in the opposite direction to Karius's far post and giving Mainz the lead. Karius was called into action again in the 35th minute after Becker beat Timo Becker down the left and pulled the ball back for Tietz, whose powerful effort from around 13 metres was brilliantly saved by the Schalke goalkeeper. The hosts remained largely ineffective in attack, leaving Mainz with a one-goal advantage at the interval. The second half continued at the same pace, with Mainz controlling proceedings with and without the ball, while Schalke struggled in the final third - unaided when Džeko was forced off after an aerial collision. Finishing with an xG of just 0.29, Schalke's wait for a home goal in the Bundesliga continues, while Mainz's excellent away run goes on. Die Nullfünfer jump to fifth in the standings for now, while Schalke remain in the bottom half on five points, though their goal record of just four continues to be a concern.

item.title: Ceddanne Rafaela, Wilyer Abreu, Caleb Durbin finalists for Gold Gl0ve
item.description: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - MAY 12: Caleb Durbin #5 of the Boston Red Sox, Ceddanne Rafaela #3 of the Boston Red Sox, and Wilyer Abreu #52 of the Boston Red Sox react in the dugout before a game agains the the Philadelphia Phillies on May 12, 2026 at Fenway Park in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Malhotra/Boston Red Sox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Gold Glove nominations were announced this week, with three Red Sox players landing on the list. You already know exactly who they are, even if you hadn’t heard the news: Ceddanne Rafaela, Wilyer Abreu, and Caleb Durbin. Having 33% of your defense made up of young, defensively elite players is a great thing, even if two of those players still have plenty of question marks about their offensive profiles. But will any of them take home the hardware this year, and do any of them have a chance at taking home the Platinum Glove, which goes to the best fielder in each league regardless of position? Let’s take a look. Ceddanne Rafaela Rafaela and Pete Crowe-Armstong are probably going to battle for the title of Baseball’s Best Defensive Centerfielder for the next decade. But for this year at least, PCA finished pretty far out in front by Fielding Run Value, posting a league-leading 26 Outs-above-average compared to Ceddanne’s ninth-place (second-place amongst oufielders) 16. But PCA plays in the National League, of course. Ceddy’s 16 OAA were tops amongst all AL outfielders, and were third overall in the AL behind two shortstops: Bobby Witt, Jr. (24) and Ezequiel Duran (17). ‘Nuff Cedd made six plays that had a catch probability of 10% or less. Here’s the one that required him to cover the most distance in the least amount of time, 76 feet in 4.1 seconds: View Link Wilyer Abreu Wilyer Abretu finished with just 2 OAA this year, significantly down from last year’s 8 and just 41st among all outfielders. He didn’t make a single play with a catch probability below 20%, let alone the several five-percenters that Ceddanne tracked down. But we all know that range isn’t Wilyer’s best defensive attribute, his arm is. For my money, this is the prettiest throw he uncorked all season: View Link So, with his OAA numbers not looking so hot, Abreu is going to struggle to defend his Gold Glove and has no shot at the Platinum, right? Not so fast. OAA is just one of two primary defensive stats currently en vogue amongst people who chatter about baseball on the internet. The other one is Defensive Runs Saved. And guess what? Abreu led all of baseball this year with 28 in that category. He finished 5 DRS ahead of second-place Bryce Turang, 7 ahead of his teammate Ceddanne Rafaela, and a whopping 12 ahead of PCA. How could these two metrics, both of which purport to provide a wholistic measurement of a player’s fielding value, be so different and which one is better? Absolutely no one knows! Everyone merely choses which one to use based on which one does a better job proving whatever point they are actively trying to make. Cal

item.title: 3 Things to Watch in Chargers-Chiefs: Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston are good to go in Week 6
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Defensive co-ordinator Chris O'Leary and inside linebacker coach Sean Spence of the Los Angeles Chargers celebrate a stop of the Los Angeles Rams on fourth and goal during the first half in a preseason game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s Chargers-Chiefs this week and as much as I’d like to be able to say this one is for sole possession of first place in the AFC West, I cannot. One team is winless and the other is undefeated. This one does not look good on paper. By records alone, it also doesn’t look like a fun watch for anyone that isn’t already a fan of either team. But hey, it’s a divisional matchup that has given us plenty of entertaining watches over the last decade. More than likely this one will still do the same. That said, here are three things I’ll be watching closely when these teams take the field on Sunday. 1.) What will the offense look like just one week before the bye? There’s a very strong chance the Chargers simply play it safe with their numerous injuries and use this week as one more opportunity to see what the bottom of the roster has within them. Wide receivers Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston, and Brenen Thompson are all hobbled and have been limited through the first two practices this week. Tre’ Harris is in even worse shape as he has been a DNP thus far. KeAndre Lambert-Smith just had his 21-day window activated and it looks like he’s trending to return this week. That development may lead the Chargers to take a cautious approach with their top guys just one week from the bye. Let’s just be honest, the offense honestly looks no better no matter who is out there unless it’s a healthy McConkey. He hasn’t been healthy since Week One and it’s about time we let him get to 100 percent before he steps back out on the field. Right now, Justin Herbert’s healthy receivers are Theo Wease, Derius Davis, and Marquez Valdez-Scantling. On the practice squad, they have Gary Jennings and the recently-signed Luke Grimm. Jennings is out of game day elevations which means he’d have to be signed to the active roster in order to participate against the Chiefs. With Alec Ingold now on IR, Jennings could take that spot if the team chooses. As for the offensive line, will they send out four rookies for another week? Will veteran Daniel Brunskill learn the offense enough to start at right tackle for Alex Harkey? We’ll have to see come game day. UPDATE: Both Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston were removed from the final injury report meaning Justin Herbert will have his two top wideouts back this Sunday. 2.) Will Omarion Hampton continue to see his snaps share decrease? Hampton played only 31.7 percent of the offense’s snaps against the Broncos, although he did receive over 40 percent of the running back carries. With each week, Hampton is playing less and less. Kimani Vidal
item.content:encoded: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Defensive co-ordinator Chris O'Leary and inside linebacker coach Sean Spence of the Los Angeles Chargers celebrate a stop of the Los Angeles Rams on fourth and goal during the first half in a preseason game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s Chargers-Chiefs this week and as much as I’d like to be able to say this one is for sole possession of first place in the AFC West, I cannot. One team is winless and the other is undefeated. This one does not look good on paper. By records alone, it also doesn’t look like a fun watch for anyone that isn’t already a fan of either team. But hey, it’s a divisional matchup that has given us plenty of entertaining watches over the last decade. More than likely this one will still do the same. That said, here are three things I’ll be watching closely when these teams take the field on Sunday. 1.) What will the offense look like just one week before the bye? There’s a very strong chance the Chargers simply play it safe with their numerous injuries and use this week as one more opportunity to see what the bottom of the roster has within them. Wide receivers Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston, and Brenen Thompson are all hobbled and have been limited through the first two practices this week. Tre’ Harris is in even worse shape as he has been a DNP thus far. KeAndre Lambert-Smith just had his 21-day window activated and it looks like he’s trending to return this week. That development may lead the Chargers to take a cautious approach with their top guys just one week from the bye. Let’s just be honest, the offense honestly looks no better no matter who is out there unless it’s a healthy McConkey. He hasn’t been healthy since Week One and it’s about time we let him get to 100 percent before he steps back out on the field. Right now, Justin Herbert’s healthy receivers are Theo Wease, Derius Davis, and Marquez Valdez-Scantling. On the practice squad, they have Gary Jennings and the recently-signed Luke Grimm. Jennings is out of game day elevations which means he’d have to be signed to the active roster in order to participate against the Chiefs. With Alec Ingold now on IR, Jennings could take that spot if the team chooses. As for the offensive line, will they send out four rookies for another week? Will veteran Daniel Brunskill learn the offense enough to start at right tackle for Alex Harkey? We’ll have to see come game day. UPDATE: Both Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston were removed from the final injury report meaning Justin Herbert will have his two top wideouts back this Sunday. 2.) Will Omarion Hampton continue to see his snaps share decrease? Hampton played only 31.7 percent of the offense’s snaps against the Broncos, although he did receive over 40 percent of the running back carries. With each week, Hampton is playing less and less. Kimani Vidal’s huge 42-yard touchdown rumble will not do him any favors in getting back anywhere lose to workhorse duties. It also doesn’t help that Mike McDaniel continues to force Keaton Mitchell into the game plan to run sweeps to specifically the right side. Defenses know what’s coming when either back is in, which can’t be good for a Chargers offense that already isn’t fooling anyone in anyway. The Chiefs have a great defense. Their linebackers can fly, hit hard, and blitz. Chris Jones is still a menace along the interior and George Karlaftis is an ascending pass rusher. They’re about to face a very young Chargers offensive line and it may not even matter which running back is in. Hampton, in my opinion, is still the Chargers’ most talented back. I don’t think he’s a timeshare guy and his ability to punish deep into the fourth quarter was an aid to the Bolts last season as they closed out games with the ball in their hands. It’d be nice to get back to that kind of football. But seeing how things are going, we may never see that again (at least, maybe until next year?). 3.) Can Chris O’Leary’s defense continue their strong start against another elite offense? After a rough outing in Week One against the Cardinals, O’Leary’s unit has been one of the best in the entire league the past four weeks. Check out these numbers: Chris O’Leary’s #Chargers defense over the last 4 games: – 5th in EPA/play – 7th in success rate – 5th in dropback/EPA – 11th in EPA/rush – 6th in dropback success rate – 14th in rushing success rate pic.twitter.com/agcgGawueE — Guilty As Charged Podcast (@GACPodcast17) October 12, 2026 Despite not having Derwin James and Donte Jackson in their past two games, they’re still a top-1o unit in EPA/play, success rate, and dropback/EPA. The efficiency is insane for a group that’s far and away the leader in most drives started within their own territory (18!). Compared to the Saints who are second with 11, that’s even more unreal. They got Josh Allen and the Bills to turn the ball over five times and helped put a lid on both Sam Darnold and Bo Nix the past two weeks. Now they will face Patrick Mahomes and the revitalized Chiefs offense that now features Kenneth Walker and a highly-productive rushing attack. O’Leary doesn’t need the team to win this game for it to be a personal “W” in his book. If the defense does their part, records a turnover or two, and helps keep this one close, no one will be able to say another word about his group not pulling their weight.

item.title: ‘We’ve Let Our Fans Down’ — Titans CEO Makes Feelings Clear on Tennessee’s 0–5 Start, Robert Saleh’s Future As HC
item.description: ‘We’ve Let Our Fans Down’ — Titans CEO Makes Feelings Clear on Tennessee’s 0–5 Start, Robert Saleh’s Future As HC The Tennessee Titans are among the three NFL teams still searching for their first victory of the season. Robert Saleh’s first season as head coach has undoubtedly become a frustrating experience for fans. However, Titans CEO Burke Nihill understands the frustration and anger among the fan base while continuing to express his support for head coach Robert Saleh and general manager Mike Borgonzi. Titans CEO Addresses Fans’ Anger After Tennessee’s Disastrous Start The Titans’ offensive struggles have been a major factor behind their winless start. Tennessee ranks last in PFN’s NFL Offense Impact rankings, earning a grade of just 67.9. The team’s latest loss once again exposed their offensive struggles. Tennessee suffered a disappointing 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans in Week 5, managing just 187 total yards. During an interview with ESPN on Friday, Nihill addressed fans’ disappointment and accepted responsibility for the team’s inability to deliver better results. “The first thing I would say back to the fans is just that we’re sorry,” Nihill said . “There’s nobody in this building that doesn’t feel a sense of grief about it, because not only are we fans of the team as well, but we feel the sense of responsibility to deliver. And we’ve let our fans down because football is supposed to be fun.” BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator The franchise is coming off two consecutive 3-14 seasons. Now, the latest defeat dropped the Titans to fourth place in the AFC South with a 0-5 record. However, when a team opens a season with five consecutive losses, questions about the head coach’s future become difficult to avoid. Those concerns are particularly significant in Tennessee, where the franchise fired at least one coach or general manager in each calendar year from 2022 through 2025. Despite the pressure surrounding the team’s winless start, Nihill remains confident in Saleh and Borgonzi. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer “I believe that Mike Borgonzi and Robert Saleh are ultimately going to get this team out of the woods and restore it to competitive football,” he said. “The train is on the tracks. It just hasn’t picked up momentum, but it will.” The Titans CEO added, “I can confidently say this organization is in a place where there is organizational belief in Mike, in Robert, and they absolutely have all the support they need to get this train moving and moving faster.” The Titans’ supporters are waiting for more than an apology. They want to see progress, and, above all, their first win of the 2026 NFL season. Tennessee will now turn its attention to its upcoming matchup against the Indianapolis Colts, hoping to end its losing streak and finally give its frustrated fan base something to celebrate. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Timberwolves get major reality check despite LaMelo Ball, Anthony Edwards pairing from former head coach
item.description: © Sam Sharpe-Imagn Images Timberwolves get major reality check despite LaMelo Ball, Anthony Edwards pairing from former head coach appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Minnesota Timberwolves enter the 2026-27 NBA season with one of the league’s most intriguing backcourts following the acquisition of LaMelo Ball to pair with Anthony Edwards. However, former NBA head coach Tyrone Corbin believes Minnesota’s championship aspirations will ultimately depend on its defense rather than its offensive firepower. Speaking with Kyle Odegard of NEXTPredict, Corbin expressed confidence in Ball and Edwards developing chemistry but questioned whether the Timberwolves can consistently slow opposing teams. “They’re going to have to get some stops at some point. Offensively, you look at the talent they’ll have on the floor in those two guys alone, they’re going to be able to score the ball. Do they have enough to figure out how to slow other teams?” Corbin said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “There are some nights you just can’t force your will on a team, and defense will save you. With Rudy Gobert anchoring in there I hope it will help some, but they’re going to need to stay in front of their guys at some point.” Minnesota finished its preseason with a 3-3 record, including a 133-116 loss to the Chicago Bulls on Friday night. Despite his defensive concerns, Corbin expects Ball and Edwards to complement each other offensively. “Easy. They both are dynamic offensive talents. LaMelo can score from anywhere but he can really pass the ball. You have to make sure the guys on the floor with him are looking, because he will throw it from anywhere and get it there.” Tyrone Corbin believes LaMelo Ball, Anthony Edwards can thrive together Ball’s arrival gives Edwards another established offensive creator capable of generating scoring opportunities for himself and his teammates. Corbin also believes their personalities will help accelerate the adjustment. “He is a great, great young man. I think his personality, and the things I hear about Ant’s personality, is that they’ll mesh pretty quickly, and that talent on the floor will come together.” However, Minnesota faces considerable competition in a Western Conference featuring the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs . With Gobert anchoring the interior defense, the Timberwolves have an established rim protector. Still, Corbin emphasized that Minnesota’s perimeter defenders must provide sufficient resistance to maximize the team’s potential. “They’re going to be good, man. To have Edwards there, and then add a kid like LaMelo, and Rudy in the middle. With the way they’re going to be able to score, if they can get some stops, they’re going to be something to reckon with in the West.” The Timberwolves will begin their regular season Wednesday, Oct. 21, against Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Miami Heat on the road.
