item.title: Analyst Lists DK Metcalf as a Trade Target for the Colts
item.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Michael Roberts, Editor Could DK Metcalf end up with the Indianapolis Colts? Recently, Aaron Zacharias of Horseshoe Heroes wrote about wide receivers the Colts need to consider before the NFL Trade Deadline passes. Metcalf, who’s currently with the Pittsburgh Steelers , was on the list: “DK Metcalf (Pittsburgh Steelers) DK Metcalf is the least likely on this list for the Colts’ future ambitions, but he’s also the most interesting possible target. Either it’s the Aaron Rodgers factor, or he’s simply not a good fit with the Pittsburgh Steelers; Metcalf has, in any case, not worked out. There is a world where the Steelers could trade Metcalf after just one and a half seasons, or wait until they get a different quarterback next year. That said, if there is any interest in him from other teams, would the Steelers turn it away? The Colts could land a No. 1 target with actual No. 1 target experience.” Without a doubt, Indianapolis needs help at the wide receiver position. Does trading for DK Metcalf make sense? Analyst Lists DK Metcalf as a Trade Target for the Colts The Seattle Seahawks drafted DK Metcalf in the second round (64th overall pick) of the 2019 NFL Draft. As a rookie, he caught 58 passes for 900 yards and seven touchdowns. He recorded seven receptions for 160 yards and a touchdown in Seattle’s playoff win over the Philadelphia Eagles . It was the NFL record for most receiving yards by a rookie in a postseason game. In 2020, Metcalf finished with 83 receptions for 1,303 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. He also made the Pro Bowl and was named a second-team All-Pro. Metcalf finished the 2023 campaign with 66 receptions for 1,114 yards and eight touchdowns. He was named to the second Pro Bowl of his career that year. DK Metcalf was later traded to the Steelers in 2025. During his career in Pittsburgh, he has caught 78 passes for 1,075 yards and seven touchdowns. Metcalf’s production has been underwhelming this year. In five games, he has only recorded 19 catches for 225 yards and a touchdown on 37 targets. The Last Word Sep 13, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce (14) celebrates during the first quarter against the Baltimore Ravens at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images The Colts wide receiver room is not elite by any stretch of the imagination. It wouldn’t be great even if Alec Pierce was available. Pierce is currently out with a heel injury, and is reportedly still a few weeks away from returning to the field. The former Cincinnati Bearcat signed a four-year, $114 million extension with the Colts during the offseason. Pierce was supposed to be “The Man” for Indy, but he has only played in two games this season. Fellow Colts receivers like Josh Downs and newcomer Keenan Allen haven’t stepped up in Pierce’s absence. The former Cincinnati Bearcat signed a four-year, $114 million extension with the Colts during the offseason. Pierce was supposed to be “The Man” for Indy, but he has only played in two games this season. Fellow Colts receivers like Josh Downs and newcomer Keenan Allen haven’t stepped up in Pierce’s absence. The team was rumored to trade for Marvin Harrison Jr., but the Arizona Cardinals , of course, traded him to the Houston Texans instead. Should Indy trade for DK Metcalf before this year’s November 10 Trade Deadline? The Colts could use a two-time Pro Bowler like Metcalf. Yet, it’s unclear what the team would have to give up in a deal. Plus, it’s unclear whether the Steelers would even be willing to trade him. Colts quarterback Daniel Jones would surely love to add DK Metcalf. What quarterback wouldn’t want to add another offensive playmaker? Metcalf could team with tight end Tyler Warren and improve the team’s pass-catching corps. But it’s unlikely that such a trade will happen. More NFL News: Jason Kelce Calls Out Nick Sirianni’s Questionable Call in Eagles’ Loss to Jaguars Jalen Hurts’ Contract Could Become a $255 Million Problem for Philadelphia 4 Priority Issues For Dan Campbell’s 2026 Bye Week Main Image: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images

item.title: Muheim produces late magic again as Hamburg stun Stuttgart
item.description: Muheim produces late magic again as Hamburg stun Stuttgart Despite facing their third away fixture in just seven days, Sebastian Hoeneß’s Stuttgart side started brightly in Hamburg, dominated possession early, and created several promising chances. But, it was Hamburg who posed the initial attacking threat, as Fabio Vieira intercepted a misplaced pass from Angelo Stiller in the fifth minute but failed to convert, sending his shot wide of Dennis Seimen’s goal. The visitors gradually asserted themselves, with Deniz Undav meeting a delivery from Bilal El Khannouss and directing it over the crossbar with his shoulder; shortly after, Hamburg-born Ermedin Demirovic headed another cross from the Moroccan wide in the 15th minute. Stuttgart dominated possession in the opening stages, holding over 80%, but Merlin Polzin’s side grew into the contest and nearly took the lead in the 27th minute when a corner from Miro Muheim found Sebastian Bornauw, whose header deflected off Vieira and Seimen made an impressive save. The visitors kept the pressure on and came closest to breaking the deadlock six minutes before the interval, as a well-executed counterattack let Jamie Leweling pick out Undav in the penalty area, but the Stuttgart captain’s first-time effort hit the post. Demirovic then saw a header denied by Daniel Heuer Fernandes, ensuring that both teams entered the interval goalless. Yousuff Poulsen nearly scored for the hosts three minutes into the second half, striking the post following a lofted pass from David Moller Wolfe. As in previous fixtures in Paderborn and Bratislava, Stuttgart sought to regain control early in the second half, though Hamburg had begun to gain the upper hand. Six minutes after his earlier attempt, Poulsen came closest to scoring, his shot striking the bar after a touch from VfB goalkeeper Seimen, while less than a minute earlier, Demirovic had sent a header just inches wide. As has been the theme of the season, the match became an end-to-end contest after Stuttgart's early dominance, with HSV looking increasingly threatening. They had an effort in the 58th minute when Undav attempted an acrobatic volley that Heuer Fernandes denied, as the half continued at a frenetic pace and the Volksparkstadion anticipated the opening goal. Heading into the weekend, a point would have been perfect for HSV, but they could well have sensed a missed opportunity in the second half had they not found the net. In the 88th minute, they finally punished Stuttgart, with Muheim hammering in from range and catching Seimen off guard with a ripper, his second late strike in a week after netting against Hoffenheim last time out. For Stuttgart, it is hard to argue that anything other than defeat was deserved. Once again, they surrendered control in the second half and struggled to get a grip as the pace increased. item.title: Füllkrug's second-half brace rescues draw for Bremen against Paderborn
item.description: Füllkrug's second-half brace rescues draw for Bremen against Paderborn Werder Bremen had to battle back and save parity against a clinical SC Paderborn this afternoon at the Weserstadion. Two first-half goals from the visitors made for a chorus of whistles at the interval, but Niclas Füllkrug's brace ensured a share of the spoils. Making home advantage count in the initial exchanges, it seemed near inevitable that Bremen would open the scoring as Niclas Füllkrug flashed wide. Minutes later, only Nahuel Noll stood between Marco Grüll and Chucki from reasonably gilt-edged positions. In a blink of an eye, however, Paderborn established a 2-0 lead. Grüll's mix up on the ball allowed Steffen Tigges to feed Stefano Marino. The 22-year-old driving into the right side of the box with speed before arrowing the ball into Karl Hein's top-right corner. Things got even better for Ralf Rangnick's men when Tigges himself netted on the half-hour. Bremen's rearguard were caught napping, letting a long throw bounce into the box for a routine toe-poke finish. Another Noll parry crucially kept out Arthur before the interval. Making one change at the breeak, Daniel Thioune's side halved the deficit just before the hour. A diagonal ball flicked on by Eren Dincki sat up nicely for Niclas Füllkrug to snap the ball inside the lower-left post. Suddenly the half-time boos made way for support. Mitchell Weiser's bench impact proved telling 7 minute later. His cross yielded a penalty after Laurin Curda's handball. Füllkrug stuck it away to take his season tally up to six. Paderborn also emptied the bench, bringing on Pieringer, Baack, Phillipe and Müller Bremen pushed to complete the comeback with Weiser and Arthur testing Noll from tight angles. Paderborn also had their chances to snatch it late on. Four minutes of injury time left Rayan Philippe with a shot that struck the post and bounced ensuring it stayed a draw.

item.title: Luis Enrique rolls the dice with heavily changed team against Strasbourg
item.description: Luis Enrique rolls the dice with heavily changed team against Strasbourg PSG have rotated their team heavily to take on Strasbourg in Ligue 1 this afternoon, with a largely second string on the pitch. If you enjoy PSG Talk coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. It’s become almost impossible to guess Luis Enrique’s starting XIs for Ligue 1 games. The coach loves to rotate in these domestic games, and he’s constantly keeping people guessing with his moves through the whole team. The fact that he has such good options in every position means he can vary the lineup massively without losing any strength. PSG rotate heavily for trip to Alsace Maghnes Akliouche scores his first PSG goal. (Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images) For today’s game against Strasbourg, it was known in advance that Marquinhos wasn’t going to play. But his changes have actually gone much further than that. It’s as close to a second string as you’ll see from the coach. Of course Tuesday night’s game against Barcelona is a huge factor in his thinking. Ousmane Dembele, Desire Doue, Fabian Ruiz, Vitinha, Nuno Mendes, Willian Pacho and Achraf Hakimi jointheir captain Marquinhos in missing out. That means the team has Matvey Safonov in goal, with a back four featuring Lucas Digne and Warren Zaire Emery at full back, with Ilya Zabarnyi and Lucas Hernandez at centre back. In midfield, Dro Fernandez makes his latest appearance, alongside Joao Neves. It looks like Lucas Beraldo will sit behind them. The front three has Ferran Torres leading the line, flanked by Khvicha Kvaratshelia and Maghnes Akliouche. That is a team that is still packed with world class quality, despite the rotation. In other news… Marquinhos is not in the team to face Strasbourg this afternoon as Luis Enrique continues his strict rotation policy. Maghnes Akliouche probably won’t get the start today – but that doesn’t mean his manager isn’t delighted with his progress.

item.title: Who could replace Otega Oweh on two-way contract? Here are 3 candidates
item.description: After filling out their roster, the Oklahoma City Thunder could be forced to make another move before Opening Night. Under sad circumstances, unfortunately. Otega Oweh sustained a season-ending torn Achilles tendon in the NBA preseason. Now that Oweh is out for the entire 2026-27 season, that puts the Thunder in a tough spot. Sure, you liked him enough to add him with the No. 41 pick of the 2026 NBA draft. But surely, you can't keep a two-way spot occupied by someone you know won't log minutes. If the Thunder eventually waive Oweh, who could replace him on a two-way deal? The other two guys for OKC under that same contract are Brooks Barnhizer and Josh Dix. Let's look at three candidates who could eventually take Oweh's spot on the NBA roster: Christoph Tilly This is probably the safest pick. Reading the tea leaves, it seems like the Thunder really like Tilly. He was the first player signed to an Exhibit-10 deal. And so far, he's the only one of the original four who remains on OKC's roster. The other three were waived on Friday. Tilley went undrafted out of Ohio State in the 2026 NBA draft. He was part of OKC's 2026 Summer League squad. He's a seven-footer who can handle and shoot the ball well for his size. Watch out for him as a realistic option to get a two-way spot. Dariq Whitehead By a slim margin, Whitehead remains eligible for a two-way spot. He has three years of NBA experience. The 2023 first-round pick is fighting for his basketball dream. Injuries have completely destroyed them. Recently signed by OKC, it seems like the organization likes the talent and is taking a flyer on him. Whitehead spent two seasons with the Brooklyn Nets. He was on a 10-day contract with the Memphis Grizzlies last year. Before that, he was putting up numbers on the G League's OKC Blue. So there's some history there. If you're looking for headlines, this is the way to go. Most NBA fans know who he is. Milos Uzan Sometimes, you gotta go outside of your bubble. In comes Uzan. He was one of the more decorated guys to go undrafted in the 2026 NBA draft. He should be a familiar name as he spent two collegiate seasons at Oklahoma before transferring to Houston. That's where he broke out. The Cougars have been a national title contender for the last few years. He helped with that. Right now, Uzan is on the Boston Celtics under an Exhibit-10 deal. But the Thunder can easily swoop in and sign him to a two-way spot. That'd be a cool story as a former Sooner. Plus, he's played well in the preseason. He recently had 14 points in an OT win over the Philadelphia 76ers. And Kelvin Sampson usually has his guys ready to defend at the NBA level. This article originally appeared on OKC Thunder Wire: Who could replace Otega Oweh on two-way contract? Here are 3 candidates

item.description: ⚽ Updates on the Saturday afternoon football action ⚽ Live scoreboard | Tables | Top scorers | Email Simon Andy Hunter’s match report from the Hill Dickinson is here, and you can find it below. Chelsea have returned from the international break with an authority that augurs well for Xabi Alonso. A brace from Pedro Neto condemned Everton to an inaugural defeat of the season as the visitors climbed to fourth on the back of their first Premier League clean sheet since January. A head injury sustained by Emi Martínez, who was carried off on a stretcher after seven minutes of treatment, was the only concern from a mature display in the Merseyside sunshine for Alonso’s team. There were goalkeeping issues at both ends of the field with Jordan Pickford unconvincing for the second week in succession as David Moyes’ side suffered self-inflicted wounds. But Everton could have no complaints about the merits of Chelsea’s victory given their contrasting performances in the second half. Continue reading...

item.title: Why isn't Nico lamaleava playing for UCLA? Bruins QB out for season after injury
item.description: Why isn't Nico lamaleava playing for UCLA? Bruins QB out for season after injury originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The 12th-ranked UCLA football team is off to an impressive start under head coach Bob Chesney. But the Bruins will have to continue without starting quarterback Nico lamaleava. The former five-star quarterback is out for the remainder of the season after suffering a knee injury in UCLA's victory over Oregon last week. The injury is a significant setback for the undefeated Bruins, who entered the week with a 5-0 record. With unprecedented postseason hopes on the line, UCLA must now adjust its offense as it prepares to face Wisconsin on Saturday. Iamaleava injured his left knee late in the second quarter against Oregon. He was tackled by Bear Alexander and Jerry Mixon while scrambling, with his leg appearing to twist during the play. UCLA's medical staff attended to the quarterback, who returned for one more play and threw an interception. However, he did not return to the field after halftime and was later seen without his uniform. Although UCLA had not officially confirmed his status earlier this week, Chesney acknowledged there was "serious concern" about the quarterback's condition. Iamaleava's absence leaves a significant gap in UCLA's offense. His ability to extend plays has helped the Bruins escape difficult situations, while his mobility forces opposing defenses to account for the passing game. This also creates opportunities for the rushing attack. He finishes the season with 982 passing yards, four touchdowns and four interceptions on 72-of-116 passing. He also recorded 144 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown. UCLA has two possible replacements for Iamaleava. Cal Poly transfer Ty Dieffenbach and Nico's younger brother, Madden lamaleava. Dieffenbach replaced the injured starter against Oregon, completing three of six passes for 43 yards and a touchdown. Chesney indicated that Dieffenbach would get an opportunity to start against Wisconsin. This also creates opportunities for the rushing attack. He finishes the season with 982 passing yards, four touchdowns and four interceptions on 72-of-116 passing. He also recorded 144 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown. UCLA has two possible replacements for Iamaleava. Cal Poly transfer Ty Dieffenbach and Nico's younger brother, Madden lamaleava. Dieffenbach replaced the injured starter against Oregon, completing three of six passes for 43 yards and a touchdown. Chesney indicated that Dieffenbach would get an opportunity to start against Wisconsin. item.title: Arsenal star pushing for January exit after recent struggles
item.description: Arsenal star pushing for January exit after recent struggles Viktor Gyokeres and Arsenal Facing January Crossroads as Exit Talk Grows Arsenal may be heading towards one of the most awkward transfer subplots of the coming window, with Viktor Gyokeres increasingly unsettled and a January move now described as a genuine possibility. According to TeamTalk , the Sweden international is prepared to reassess his future after a rapid change in standing under Mikel Arteta. The striking part of this developing story is the speed of the shift. Gyokeres arrived from Sporting CP in 2025 amid significant expectation, after Arsenal chose him ahead of Benjamin Sesko. He then delivered in a major way, scoring 21 goals in all competitions, including 14 in the Premier League, and playing his part in a title-winning season as well as a run to the Champions League final. That return should have strengthened his place. Instead, the current picture appears very different. TeamTalk states that “Viktor Gyokeres is ready to quit Arsenal and is set to push for a January exit”, a line that underlines the seriousness of the situation. The report adds that frustration over his minutes is central, with the striker “yet to start a Premier League game this season”. Premier League starts at centre of Arsenal concern From the player’s perspective, the issue seems straightforward. A striker of Gyokeres’ profile and age does not want to drift through the first half of a season waiting for opportunities. Sources cited in the report say “his lack of opportunities is the main reason he is now looking towards the exit door”, and there is little ambiguity in that. Photo IMAGO Arsenal’s internal thinking may be more layered. Kai Havertz is “currently the preferred option”, while long-term admiration for Julian Alvarez remains active in the background. The report notes that Arsenal’s pursuit of Alvarez over the summer was “a development that could not be ignored by Gyokeres and his camp”. For a centre-forward already fighting for starts, that pursuit naturally sends a message, whether intended or not. It is also notable that Arsenal are said to be open to doing more business in attack. TeamTalk reports that the club “could be prepared to consider allowing Gyokeres to leave as they continue pushing ahead with plans to bring in another forward”. item.content:encoded: Arsenal star pushing for January exit after recent struggles Viktor Gyokeres and Arsenal Facing January Crossroads as Exit Talk Grows Arsenal may be heading towards one of the most awkward transfer subplots of the coming window, with Viktor Gyokeres increasingly unsettled and a January move now described as a genuine possibility. According to TeamTalk , the Sweden international is prepared to reassess his future after a rapid change in standing under Mikel Arteta. The striking part of this developing story is the speed of the shift. Gyokeres arrived from Sporting CP in 2025 amid significant expectation, after Arsenal chose him ahead of Benjamin Sesko. He then delivered in a major way, scoring 21 goals in all competitions, including 14 in the Premier League, and playing his part in a title-winning season as well as a run to the Champions League final. That return should have strengthened his place. Instead, the current picture appears very different. TeamTalk states that “Viktor Gyokeres is ready to quit Arsenal and is set to push for a January exit”, a line that underlines the seriousness of the situation. The report adds that frustration over his minutes is central, with the striker “yet to start a Premier League game this season”. Premier League starts at centre of Arsenal concern From the player’s perspective, the issue seems straightforward. A striker of Gyokeres’ profile and age does not want to drift through the first half of a season waiting for opportunities. Sources cited in the report say “his lack of opportunities is the main reason he is now looking towards the exit door”, and there is little ambiguity in that. Photo IMAGO Arsenal’s internal thinking may be more layered. Kai Havertz is “currently the preferred option”, while long-term admiration for Julian Alvarez remains active in the background. The report notes that Arsenal’s pursuit of Alvarez over the summer was “a development that could not be ignored by Gyokeres and his camp”. For a centre-forward already fighting for starts, that pursuit naturally sends a message, whether intended or not. It is also notable that Arsenal are said to be open to doing more business in attack. TeamTalk reports that the club “could be prepared to consider allowing Gyokeres to leave as they continue pushing ahead with plans to bring in another forward”. If that proves accurate, this is no longer a story about one unhappy player alone. It becomes a structural squad decision. Julian Alvarez interest adds to transfer pressure Arsenal “remain hugely keen on Alvarez”, according to the report, and that ongoing interest appears to be one of the two key drivers behind Gyokeres’ current stance, along with the absence of Premier League starts. In practical terms, a striker can accept competition. What becomes harder to accept is the sense that the club may already be planning for somebody else to lead the line. That is why this situation feels significant. Arsenal “spent months doing their homework on Gyokeres” before completing the move, and Arteta had been clear in wanting him in north London. For that level of planning to lead to this uncertainty little more than a year later would raise fair questions over recruitment alignment and squad planning. Gyokeres has done his part internationally, too. He “continues to score regularly for Sweden and struck four goals during the recent Nations League international break”. That form only sharpens the player’s likely belief that he should be starting more often at club level. Atletico Madrid and Europe monitoring Gyokeres situation As for the market, Atletico Madrid remain firmly in the frame. TeamTalk says the Spanish club’s interest was discussed directly with Arsenal during meetings involving Andrea Berta in the summer. There is also mention of interest from the Premier League, Italy and Germany, suggesting this is not a case of one option or nothing. Crucially, the pieces do appear to fit. The report says “with the player open to a departure and the club still keen to strengthen their attacking options, a January separation could suit both parties”. That may ultimately be the clearest line in the entire update. If both sides see logic in a split, the coming months could be about shaping the right deal rather than preventing an exit. Arsenal still have time to change the direction of this story. More starts, a clearer role and firmer communication would help. For now, though, Viktor Gyokeres, Arsenal and a possible January transfer are moving into a space worth watching very closely. Our View From an Arsenal supporter’s perspective, this is deeply frustrating because it feels like a familiar problem of our own making. We signed a striker with pedigree, backed him after a long process, watched him score 21 goals in a huge season, then somehow reached a point where “the striker is yet to start a Premier League game this season”. That is hard to defend. If the report is accurate, the most annoying part is the mixed messaging. You cannot push for a player, pick him ahead of other targets, celebrate the decision, then spend the next window chasing another elite forward and expect there to be no consequences. Of course Gyokeres and his camp would question where he stands. Any player would. There is also a bigger concern for Arsenal here. Elite clubs need strong competition, but they also need clarity. If Kai Havertz is the preferred option, say it through selection. If Gyokeres is genuinely valued, use him properly. Letting a proven goalscorer slide towards the exit after one strong season would feel wasteful and short-sighted. Supporters will rightly ask why a player who helped deliver the title now seems expendable so quickly. If Arsenal sell in January and then spend heavily again, it will look like another expensive correction rather than a clear plan. That is the part fans will struggle with most.

item.title: Venezia upset Napoli for first Serie A win of season
item.description: Venezia goalkeeper saves a penalty from Napoli's Kevin de Bruyne (ANDREA PATTARO) Napoli's torrid start to the season continued Saturday when Venezia head coach Davide Nicola masterminded a shock 1-0 win on debut as Kevin De Bruyne had a penalty saved. Renowned survival specialist Nicola was appointed during the week to replace sacked coach Giovanni Stroppa after last season's Serie B champions failed to pick up a single point in their opening six games. He made an instant impact as Akor Adams struck the winner early in the second half to seal Venezia's first Serie A win over Napoli since 1942. It marked a second defeat in a row for Massimiliano Allegri's side after their midweek Champions League loss at Villarreal, and their fifth defeat in nine games in all competitions this season. A flat game came to life early in the second half when Nigeria international Adams latched on to a long ball and beat Alex Meret with a deflected strike in the 49th minute. Allegri responded by bringing on rested stars Rasmus Hojlund and Kevin De Bruyne and the Danish striker immediately threatened when Juan Jesus denied him a tap-in with a superb goal-line block. Hojlund won a penalty for Napoli midway through the second half when he was hauled down in the box by Matias Moreno, but De Bruyne's spot-kick was well saved by Filip Stankovic low to his right. The Venezia goalkeeper, son of former Inter midfielder Dejan Stankovic, was decisive in the closing stages with a string of saves, including spectacular stops to deny Stanislav Lobotka and Alisson Santos. Napoli are ninth after picking up 10 points from their first seven games, while Venezia remain bottom with three points. Later on Saturday, league leaders Inter travel to Bologna before Roma host Genoa. str/pb

item.title: NFL draft prospects 2027: Players to watch for Florida State vs. Miami
item.description: CLEMSON, SOUTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 03: Darian Mensah #10 of the Miami Hurricanes warms up during the first half of a football game against the Clemson Tigers at Memorial Stadium on October 03, 2026 in Clemson, South Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 7 of the college football season is here, and it brings a key Florida in-state rivalry game. The Florida State Seminoles head from Tallahassee to South Florida today to face the Miami Hurricanes. This game obviously has plenty of meaning for our community, with so many people having attended or become fans of either team. It felt like the right time to bring in the Miami Dolphins’ perspective and take a closer look at some of the 2027 NFL Draft prospects who could be on the field today. The game kicks off at 7 p.m. Eastern on ESPN and Disney+. Florida State 2027 Draft prospects Duce Robinson, wide receiver (Senior) – Robinson is a huge target – like a bigger-than-the-Dolphins-tight-ends huge target. Listed at 6-foot-6 and 230 pounds, Robinson uses his size to give his quarterback a receiver who will fight for contested passes in a huge catch radius. If he gets his hands on the ball, it is going to be a catch. He is not the most precise route runner, and he does not have the speed to pull away from anyone, so he relies on his size to make the catch rather than speed to create separation. He is probably a day-two prospect who can excel as a possession receiver and redzone target. Charles Lester III, cornerback (Junior) – Lester is likely a developmental outside cornerback with good size. He is 6-foot-2 and 195 pounds, but he still needs to develop his technique, especially against faster, smaller wide receivers. He needs to clean up his work when receivers cut, but he can coach that up this year and in the NFL. He still has eligibility, so a 2027 return to college is not out of the question, but he could transition to the league, probably as a day-two pick. For Miami, where cornerback depth is a question mark, Lester could be an ideal option. Ja’Bril Rawls, cornerback (Senior) – Another cornerback with good size (6-foot-1, 180 pounds), Rawls is behind his teammate in draft potential, but the potential for success in the NFL is there. He probably needs to add strength, and his frame suggests he can do that without sacrificing speed. He has the versatility to slide back to safety, which might be the better option. He is not the best tackler, and he will need to clean that up in the NFL, especially if he is expected to step up in run defense. A developmental defensive back option who should contribute on special teams, Rawls is likely a day-three prospect who could rise to the end of day two. Quintrevion Wisner, running back (Senior) – The former Texas running back moved to Florida State this year after three seasons in Austin. He carried the ball 226 times for 1,064 yards in 2024, but he played only nine games in 2025 due to a hamstring injury. He has 29 carries for 141 yar
item.content:encoded: CLEMSON, SOUTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 03: Darian Mensah #10 of the Miami Hurricanes warms up during the first half of a football game against the Clemson Tigers at Memorial Stadium on October 03, 2026 in Clemson, South Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 7 of the college football season is here, and it brings a key Florida in-state rivalry game. The Florida State Seminoles head from Tallahassee to South Florida today to face the Miami Hurricanes. This game obviously has plenty of meaning for our community, with so many people having attended or become fans of either team. It felt like the right time to bring in the Miami Dolphins’ perspective and take a closer look at some of the 2027 NFL Draft prospects who could be on the field today. The game kicks off at 7 p.m. Eastern on ESPN and Disney+. Florida State 2027 Draft prospects Duce Robinson, wide receiver (Senior) – Robinson is a huge target – like a bigger-than-the-Dolphins-tight-ends huge target. Listed at 6-foot-6 and 230 pounds, Robinson uses his size to give his quarterback a receiver who will fight for contested passes in a huge catch radius. If he gets his hands on the ball, it is going to be a catch. He is not the most precise route runner, and he does not have the speed to pull away from anyone, so he relies on his size to make the catch rather than speed to create separation. He is probably a day-two prospect who can excel as a possession receiver and redzone target. Charles Lester III, cornerback (Junior) – Lester is likely a developmental outside cornerback with good size. He is 6-foot-2 and 195 pounds, but he still needs to develop his technique, especially against faster, smaller wide receivers. He needs to clean up his work when receivers cut, but he can coach that up this year and in the NFL. He still has eligibility, so a 2027 return to college is not out of the question, but he could transition to the league, probably as a day-two pick. For Miami, where cornerback depth is a question mark, Lester could be an ideal option. Ja’Bril Rawls, cornerback (Senior) – Another cornerback with good size (6-foot-1, 180 pounds), Rawls is behind his teammate in draft potential, but the potential for success in the NFL is there. He probably needs to add strength, and his frame suggests he can do that without sacrificing speed. He has the versatility to slide back to safety, which might be the better option. He is not the best tackler, and he will need to clean that up in the NFL, especially if he is expected to step up in run defense. A developmental defensive back option who should contribute on special teams, Rawls is likely a day-three prospect who could rise to the end of day two. Quintrevion Wisner, running back (Senior) – The former Texas running back moved to Florida State this year after three seasons in Austin. He carried the ball 226 times for 1,064 yards in 2024, but he played only nine games in 2025 due to a hamstring injury. He has 29 carries for 141 yards this season, but is buried on the depth chart, and he has to prove he can be a receiving option out of the backfield before he can be considered a feature running back at the NFL level. He is a day-three depth running back option who can contribute on special teams. Micahi Danzy, wide receiver (Redshirt sophomore) – Danzy is the smaller receiver on our FSU prospects list, but that is only because Robinson is ridiculously large. Danzy is listed at 6-foot-1 and 195 pounds, and he can line up in multiple roles among the receiving corps. He has track speed, setting the FSU school record in the 400, and started his college career as a running back. He has 19 receptions for 139 yards and two touchdowns this season. He uses his speed to his advantage but needs to keep building his route tree. He is probably a day-three prospect who could use his speed to battle his way into a day-two consideration. Miami 2027 Draft prospects Darian Mensah, quarterback (Redshirt junior) – Mensah is a modern college football player who bounces between teams; he started at Tulane, then spent a year at Duke before moving to Miami this year. He throws with anticipation and makes good decisions, but he does not always work through his progressions and still has to prove he can handle pressure. He does not have the strongest arm and throws great short-to-medium passes, but the ball can die on longer throws at times. He could be the first quarterback off the board this year, potentially as the number one overall pick. Xavier Lucas, cornerback (Junior) – Lucas might be the ideal press-corner for the NFL. He has the size (6-foot-2, 200 pounds) to disrupt receivers at the line of scrimmage and the speed to keep up with the league’s vertical threats. He contests passes well, using his size to break up jump balls, but he is more likely to knock the ball away than to come away with an interception. He is a liability on run defense, with seemingly no interest in getting his nose into the mess in front of him; he also needs to clean up his tackling. Lucas has missed the last month of the season with an undisclosed injury, but he is expected to return for tonight’s game. He is probably a day-two prospect who is clearly not a finished product and will continue to grow in the NFL. For a Dolphins team in need of defensive secondary help, Lucas could be a key target. Note: Lucas is the basis of the lawsuit from Wisconsin against Miami. Lucas played his freshman year at Wisconsin under a two-year Name, Image, and Likeness contract. He tried to transfer to Miami for his second season, but Wisconsin refused to enter him into the transfer portal, citing his contract. Lucas dropped out of Wisconsin and enrolled at Miami without entering the NCAA’s transfer portal, and Wisconsin is alleging tampering by Miami to entice Lucas to transfer. Damon Wilson II, edge (Senior) – The Dolphins will likely be highly interested in edge rushers in the 2027 Draft, and Wilson could put himself on the board. At 6-foot-4 and 250 pounds, Wilson has the size and athleticism needed to succeed in the NFL. He uses both speed and power to attack offensive tackles, but he needs to add counter moves to get off the block if his initial move does not win. He also needs to improve his edge-setting against the run. He has the flashes to be great in the NFL, but he hasn’t shown the consistency yet. He broke out last year at Missouri with a nine-sack season, and he has tallied 3.5 sacks through the first five games this year, including 2.5 sacks against Clemson a couple of weeks ago. If he can keep up that production, he will be a second-round target who could slide into the end of the first round. Samson Okunlola, offensive tackle/guard (Redshirt Junior) – Okunlola’s potential is projected based on limited playing time at Miami. He did not get regular snaps until last year, when he rotated at left guard all season. He was clean, did not allow a sack, and showed he could be relied on in big spots. He slid out to left tackle this year, and he has been successful there as well – though he has had a penalty issue that needs to be cleaned up. He could bring that versatility to the NFL, allowing teams to use him as either a guard or tackle as needed. At 6-foot-6, 330 pounds, he still brings athleticism to the line and could be an effective mover to lead block in running situations. He is probably a day-two prospect who could start as a depth option at tackle and guard before settling into a starting role as a guard on the line. Ryan Rodriguez, center (Redshirt Senior) – A sixth-year college player, Rodriguez has played both guard and center at Miami. He has had injury issues, including needing surgery in 2022 and 2024. He is 6-foot-2 and 300 pounds, which is smaller than most NFL interior linemen, but Miami’s All-Pro center, Aaron Brewer, is 6-foot-2 and 290 pounds, so that might not be a major concern. He has to prove he can withstand the pressure of an entire season and ancho

item.title: Confirmed: Barcelona starting lineup against Real Betis – 4 changes as Flick rotates ahead of PSG
item.description: Confirmed: Barcelona starting lineup against Real Betis – 4 changes as Flick rotates ahead of PSG FC Barcelona are set to take on Real Betis at La Cartuja in La Liga in less than an hour and Hansi Flick has announced his starting lineup for this evening’s encounter. The Catalans enter the contest looking to maintain their perfect start to the league campaign, having won all eight matches so far this season. However, the fixture comes during an exceptionally demanding period for Barcelona, following their 4-1 Champions League victory over Galatasaray. It is sandwiched right inbetween that trip to Turkey and a trip to France to face PSG, before welcoming Real Madrid to the Camp Nou next weekend. Flick’s team selection has attracted particular attention, with the German tactician having to make some difficult calls to manage workload. Flick makes 4 changes against Betis In goal, Joan Garcia unsurprisingly starts for Barcelona, while Jules Kounde, Pau Cubarsi, Gerard Martin and Xavi Espart complete the defensive line. Moving into midfield, Rodri and Pedri feature alongside Fermin Lopez as Flick looks to establish control against a Betis side capable of causing problems in possession. Further forward, Lamine Yamal and Karim Adeyemi occupy the wide positions with Gabriel Jesus leading Barca’s attack. The most notable selection decision is starting Karim Adeyemi on the left instead of the in-form Anthony Gordon. Meanwhile, Jules Kounde replaces Eric at right-back and Gabriel Jesus returns to the starting line-up after a promising cameo against Galatasaray. With Barcelona facing PSG and Real Madrid in the coming days, Flick’s choices also offer an indication of how he intends to manage his squad through this important run of fixtures. Nevertheless, the immediate priority remains securing another three points and extending Barcelona’s outstanding start to the domestic season and it remains to be seen how they fare against Betis.

item.title: Fantasy Football Injury Alert: A.J. Brown Expected to Play Week 6; Fantasy Fallout for Drake Maye and Patriots
item.description: Sep 9, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; aNew England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown (1) runs a route against Seattle Seahawks cornerback Josh Jobe (29) during the second quarter at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A.J. Brown's Impending Return Changes Fantasy Landscape in New England Fantasy managers who invested heavily in the New England Patriots' passing game this offseason have spent the last month and a half navigating a turbulent landscape. When blockbuster offseason acquisition A.J. Brown suffered a high-ankle sprain in the opening quarter of Week 1 against the Seattle Seahawks, it felt like a cruel joke. Sidelined on Injured Reserve for the better part of two months, Brown left fantasy lineups scrambling and forced a heavy burden onto a patchwork receiving corps. Now, according to reports from NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, the dark cloud is lifting. The Patriots are expected to activate Brown off Injured Reserve in time for their divisional matchup against the New York Jets. After returning to practice this week and testing his ankle, the star wideout is poised to reclaim his role as the undisputed fantasy stud wide receiver of this offense. While Brown may have a bit of a pitch count that limits his upside to more of a WR2 this week, his fantasy managers absolutely have to start him. The #Patriots will likely activate WR AJ Brown off Injured Reserve to play against the #Jets on Sunday, sources say. Brown returned to practice this week after a stint on IR with a high-ankle sprain and now an anticipated return to the field. pic.twitter.com/UknZRnrv8T - Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 17, 2026 For fantasy football players, this news is an absolute earthquake. Inserting an elite, difference-making alpha back into an active offense changes the math across the entire roster. But how does this dramatic shift impact key offensive pieces like Drake Maye, Romeo Doubs, Hunter Henry, and Demario Douglas? Let's break down the fantasy fallout for Week 6. While Maye has been one of the best fantasy quarterbacks over the last two weeks, his overall upside skyrockets now that he possesses a legitimate go-to option capable of turning simple plays into explosive gains. He has legit overall QB1 upside this week. WR Romeo Doubs, New England Patriots Romeo Doubs saw an expanded target share in Brown's absence, but the production has been erratic. With Brown drawing the primary cornerback coverage, Doubs slides back into a more natural secondary role. While he will face lighter defensive coverages, his total target volume will likely decrease, converting him into a high-upside, boom-or-bust flex play for Week 6. TE Hunter Henry, New England Patriots Hunter Henry occupies a uniquely stable position amid this offensive reshuffle. Henry has quietly maintained reliable chemistry with Maye throughout the early weeks of the season, and Brown's presence on the perimeter should only help the veteran tight end. Elite wide receivers stretch defenses both vertically and laterally, opening up lucrative soft spots in the middle of the field where tight ends thrive. Henry retains his status as a steady back-end option, with his red-zone equity actually getting a boost because defenses can no longer focus solely on bracketing tight ends and slot receivers near the goal line. Consider Henry a high-end TE2 with TE1 upside this week. WR Demario Douglas, New England Patriots Meanwhile, Demario Douglas faces a more noticeable PPR floor dip. Douglas thrived on manufactured touches and short-area slot volume while the receiving room was decimated, but Brown's return eats directly into those underneath targets, turning Douglas into a game-script-dependent flex play or roster hold. Douglas belongs on the bench outside of deep fantasy leagues this week, and can be thrown back on the waiver wire in most leagues. item.title: Neto double at Everton leads Chelsea to victory marred by Martínez head injury
item.description: Chelsea have returned from the international break with a spirit, authority and resilience that augurs well for Xabi Alonso. Their troubles at Everton, not a happy hunting ground in recent years, were confined to the seven minutes Emi Martínez needed treatment for a head injury as Pedro Neto’s double delivered a deserved victory in the Merseyside sunshine. The Argentina goalkeeper was taken to hospital for tests after an accidental collision with Jarrad Branthwaite left him with suspected concussion. “When he left the stadium he was conscious,” Alonso said. “Hopefully it is not too bad but we need to wait.” A first Premier League clean sheet since January, and a second successive win since losing at Brentford before the Nations League break, were otherwise secured with a minimum of fuss in a commanding second-half performance. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

The past week has encapsulated his Liverpool career so far. In the Champions League rout of Lask he was everywhere, exploiting gaps between and behind the Austrian club’s defence and knitting together a dominant display against limited opposition. In the previous game against Manchester City , however, when Andoni Iraola needed big players to step up in the absence of Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai, Wirtz was ineffective, wasteful and withdrawn when his team were chasing the game at 0-1. item.title: Football Daily | Watford, a ‘fake news’ sacking and an apology to Elton John
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! There are only two things certain in life – death and taxes Reece James knack and Watford managerial news – and Football Daily’s bingo card lit up with both on Friday. But while Chelsea’s statement on their crocked right-back having successful knee surgery was a cut-and-paste job from the last time James was injured, the quotes by Watford manager Alessio Dionisi were much more exciting, mainly because it contained an actual apology to Elton John and the remarkable news that the club’s trigger-happy owners have not already sent the Italian the same way as an apple in Michael Owen’s house . Shall we just hand over the Bigger Cup to PSG now to ease the calendar congestion?” – Krishna Moorthy. Reading that ‘European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Infantino next year’ , I can’t be the only well informed reader to think that a certain intergalactic bin wearing member of the nobility would make a terrific candidate. Can the Big Website ‘Higher Ups’ have a word?!” – Chris Reid. Looking at the Benfica v Celtic game I was immediately drawn to the presence of two Durans. Have there been any other instances of any other bands being present in a game? Possibly in the Human League? I am hoping a Serie A game with a Scritti and a Politti … a French game with Depeche and Mode. You get the general idea” – Mike Turney. Continue reading...

item.title: Do Premier League teams really need to run more to win matches?
item.description: Pundits regularly criticise teams for not running enough but is there a link between distance covered and results? By Opta Analyst It was like clockwork. Manchester United dropped points against Tottenham and critics were quick to question their effort and application, using the team’s physical statistics to make points. Speaking on Sky Sports, Jamie Redknapp said: “There’s a pattern I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when – and the stats don’t lie – the other team runs more than you. In the Premier League right now, I feel there are a couple of non-negotiables: you’ve got to run more than the other team if you want to win, or at least get close enough that it doesn’t make that much of a difference. Tottenham ran five kilometres more than Manchester United.” Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Henderson back on Merseyside, Farke threatens more misery for Carrick and Forest are a threat to Arsenal Premier League top scorers | Follow us on TikTok A lively reception awaits the former Liverpool midfielders Jordan Henderson and Xabi Alonso at Everton and, in the case of the former, any jeers can be considered an unintentional tribute. They will speak of what the 36-year-old is able to produce now as much as what, and where, he delivered in the past. With two goals and an assist against Bournemouth last Saturday, Henderson became the oldest player to contribute directly to three goals in a Premier League game, and demonstrated his role at Chelsea is not simply to elevate standards off the pitch. His midfield partnership with Moisés Caicedo gave Alonso’s team balance and enabled the front three of Morgan Rogers, João Pedro and Cole Palmer to flourish. Their confrontation against an Everton defence that had impressed this season, only to litter the draw at Hull with costly mistakes, will provide a stern test of the hosts’ unbeaten start and may well be dictated by the veteran behind them. Andy Hunter Everton v Chelsea, Saturday 12.30pm (all times BST) Brentford v Liverpool, Saturday 3pm Fulham v Hull, Saturday 3pm Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: FC Copenhagen Women have a ‘startup-like’ brand. Now they need results
item.description: A famous name and record attendances have given FCK a platform but a difficult start in Denmark’s top-flight shows success on the pitch is not guaranteed On an August day in 2024, 5,165 fans gathered at Vanløse Idrætspark to watch FC Copenhagen (FCK) take on B73 Slagelse in their first league match. For Denmark’s most successful men’s club, with 16 league titles, it marked the realisation of their desire to establish a women’s team, through collaboration with the existing FC Damsø, and an ambitious project with aims of having a wide-reaching impact on and off the pitch. The 26 months since have brought a whirlwind of success, the club securing back-to-back promotions to reach the A-Liga. Now they are in the top division and “playing with the big dogs”, as their head of women’s football, Romaney Pinnock, coins it, and they must adapt to stay there. Continue reading...

item.title: My old teammate Miroslav Klose is bucking a trend in German coaching | Philipp Lahm
item.description: ‘Miro’, now in charge at Nürnberg, knows the value of consistency and identity in an era of tinkering coaches who did not play professionally You learn the most from the best. The Champions League winners are Paris Saint-Germain, and they could achieve a historic hat-trick this season. Since the tournament’s rebrand in 1992, they would be only the second club to accomplish this feat, after Real Madrid’s run from 2016 to 2018. I see clear parallels between the two. For Madrid, nine players started in all three of their final victories. Similarly, PSG won their two finals with virtually identical lineups. The only change came during their title defence in Budapest , where Gianluigi Donnarumma no longer featured in goal, Luis Enrique having parted ways with the Italian European champion. core players: about 70 to 85% each remaining regular starters: 50 to 60% each squad players: 40 to 45% each fringe squad places: sharing the remaining maximum of 20% Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City are suddenly box-office in age of charge-rage and mega defiance | Barney Ronay
item.description: This is by far the most interesting this club have ever been and they faced PSG, a kind of twin entity in all this as oil state glove puppets Another day, another note of unreality; another vivid and brilliant spectacle that feels as though it has been whipped together out of meringue and burnt sugar. Time flies when the world is closing in. Two weeks on, this was Manchester City’s first home game since the verdict dropped, the irrefutable body of evidence was refuted, and English football entered its state of ongoing whiplash. In the stadium this felt like watching someone dance while the world burns. This was a brilliant game pegged out around six goals , a collapse, a comeback, posts and bars struck, saved penalties, and a performance of state-of-the-art omni-football from this brilliantly high-grade Paris Saint-Germain team. Continue reading...

item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. Continue reading...

item.title: Have any footballers ended their career with more own goals than goals? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the earliest trophyless seasons, scoring off one’s backside (part II) and the origins of ‘shithousery’ Mail us with all of your questions and answers “How many professional players have ended their senior careers with more own goals than goals for their own team?” wonders Peter Clark. In the past we’ve looked at the players with the most own goals , but we haven’t looked at those who ended their professional career in debit. “Southampton cult hero Francis Benali scored only one ‘positive’ goal in his career and was legendary for banging in goal-of-the-month contenders at his own end, most notably a bullet header against Oldham in the 1993-94 season ,” writes Daz Pearce. We could only find a couple of OGs for Benali, the other being against Manchester United in 1999-2000 . But we were unable to find a comprehensive Southampton database, so there’s a chance we’ve missed some beauties. Continue reading...

item.title: Christian Pulisic is no longer a focal point for the US or Milan – and that’s OK
item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. Last year, he was involved in US friendlies against Ecuador and Australia. But this year, with Fifa having folded the October window into September, Pulisic didn’t have the chance. On Sunday, his pre-match music was O Generosa, the Serie A anthem, which he observed with a soft smile. Mark Twain’s first visit to Italy left him describing the country as “a vast museum of magnificence and misery”, and it’s a fitting summary of Pulisic’s three-plus years with Milan. The magnificence: 43 goals and 25 assists in 138 appearances. The misery: just one trophy since he arrived in July 2023, a 2025 Supercoppa Italia held in Saudi Arabia. Continue reading...

item.title: Winning is not enough for Manchester City to move on from this crisis | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. But consider his assessment of Manchester City’s 3-0 win at Liverpool on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. John Brewin Match report: Liverpool 0-3 Manchester City Match report: Crystal Palace 3-1 Nottingham Forest Match report: Hull City 2-2 Everton Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Guardian sport
item.content:encoded: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

We play a bit of Spandau Ballet, chat about the classics and his career – hanging out with Frank Sinatra and Tony Bennett. In as much as you can deduce in a 10-minute chat on Zoom, Tony seems like an absolute gent. We do always try to bring it back to sport – Tony is an Arsenal fan, there’s a bit of Arteta, Leeds at the weekend. Tony brings up Billy Bremner and suggests that my co-host Charlie Baker and I are too young to remember him playing. We are, and how wonderful to be called young. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Continue reading...

The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. item.title: Lionel Messi’s Argentina career turned football into a sacred mystery
item.description: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. item.dc:creator: Marcela Mora y Araujo
item.content:encoded: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team , she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
